If the truth be known this rebellion was, in fact, a cry from the depths of the Syrian soul against the violent injustice of French occupation.

Eventually, his reaction was explosive, ‘Shell the entire territory... destroy it!, Equip a division of the army with heavy-armaments and bomb it from end to end... show no mercy for there can be no mercy in war... torture the people... every last one of them is our enemy... let even the innocent die... let the children be burned... let the women and old men be killed... I do not care who suffers or dies.... I just want this cursed uprising suppressed.’

The terrible news reached the people and the leaders of the insurgency, by way of certain loyal patriots who seemed, outwardly, to support France. It fell on their ears like a violent thunderclap and their hearts fluttered in terror as they foresaw the destruction of their entire district before their very eyes: houses burned to the ground... the innocent become vagrants wandering the streets... children killed... women and old men slaughtered... in fact, similar to what had happened previously to al-Maliha village near Damascus... for no-one had been spared and the village had been razed to the ground.

Some people erupted in fury on hearing this news... and their bodies seemed to convulse with the tremors of revolutionary pain... while others were stunned into silence as they knew full well that they would be helpless against such a heavily-armed attack, insignificant against the might of the French forces. It would probably result in causing the French to further increase their brutal attacks on innocent people, which, in turn, would have an awful effect on their agrarian interests. What could a small district do when at the mercy of one of the greatest states? What was the solution?

To a man they thought, ‘If it were only a question of our own safety we would face it without a second thought, and become martyrs for our cause... but we must think of the defenceless women, the old people and innocent children... we do not want callous men deciding the fate of our vulnerable innocents... oh God... please show us Your Mercy... oh Al’lah... Your Mercy...!’

They remained silent holding back the tears of pain and sadness as if the slaughter was actually happening before their eyes. An air of quiet confusion prevailed across the country as they raised their hands in supplication to God, invoking Him from the depth of their hearts and begging Him to prevent this impending massacre, ‘Oh God... Your Mercy... there are old men who have been devout for their entire lives, innocent infants, and young children among us.’

This silence, filled with fervent, silent prayer, was interrupted by a voice mumbling, ‘You know that officer... that Syrian officer who helps the rebels... Sheikho... haven’t you seen and heard about his loyalty and sacrifices for his compatriots and homeland... and his secret cooperation with the rebels against France? Everybody knows how he delivered all the arms of Anjar Citadel to us and Al’lah saved him and miraculously kept him from the hands of the French... and how he stopped the advance of many expeditions to the various counties of Syria by his clever plans. Why don’t we ask his help to save us from this impasse and prevent the terrible carnage that’s about to befall all of us?’

Others replied, ‘What can he do in such a situation? And what can he achieve alone if he is up against the might and power of France? Even his best and most ingenious plans will be doomed to failure. And we must keep in mind that as a military officer under French rule, he must be careful not to reveal himself to them and oppose them directly... so we doubt that he can help us.’

The first one replied, ‘But Al’lah may see fit to relieve us at his hands... so why don’t we try, because Al’lah is the One to trust in all such matters, whether great or small? And even if we fail to make use of his wonderful abilities, the situation could not get worse than it is already.’ All of them agreed and one of them was sent immediately to speak to Mohammad Amin, the Syrian officer of whom they had been speaking.

The envoy reached the officer’s house in the evening, where he was received with kind words of encouragement, which instantly soothed his air of desperation. Officer Sheikho sat with him as he related the discussion that had taken place, and the great suffering of the Syrian hierarchy and the insurgency leaders because of this impending catastrophe.

Mohammad Amin contemplated the facts of the matter, and soon grasped the bitter reality; he listened to this dreadful news as though it was a terrible nightmare unfolding before him and wondered what the fate of the country, and its people, would be if this full-scale French military invasion went ahead, God forbid, on the French pretext that they would shell only the sites of the terrorist insurgents. They had failed to disclose that they were intent on destroying it completely, and shedding the blood of many, many innocents.

What could possibly be done to thwart this final decision taken by the cruel, murderous French government? He pondered the matter further and experienced the full bitterness of such terrible news... certainly it would be fruitless to face them, and if it did come to pass, there would be countless victims, and far more indescribable destruction than if the situation were handled in a different way.

So, Mohammad Amin resorted to Al’lah with all sincerity: the news was extremely grave as he knew well what France was capable of doing under such a trumped-up pretext.

He turned to God in supplication, ‘Oh God! How can the Syrian people escape?’ Within a few quiet moments filled with silent prayer, entreating Al’lah, a plan flashed into his mind which would ensure a way out of this terrible situation: by God’s Will. A look full of hope and confidence in God crossed his face, denoting new found optimism, for he was certain that Al’lah would repel those cruel aggressors and prevent them destroying his country.

He said to the envoy, ‘Listen to me, man... Go to your comrades at once and tell them that Officer Mohammad Amin sends them his best regards and asks you to search the entire district for a skillful artist; if you don’t have one, we know of an excellent, gifted artist; then tell him to draw and paint the best and most perfect picture of the city of Holy Jerusalem... it must be very big... then let everyone work together to fix it to the wall of the first house to be seen by all who arrive in this country; then the problem will be solved by God’s Will.’

The man replied, ‘Is that all, sir? And the problem will be solved? But how? It seems too easy.’

Mohammad Amin said, ‘As I have told you... don’t delay... carry out the plan quickly. Ask the artist to execute the work to the very best of his ability... and as quickly as possible... and remember that Al’lah is the One we trust to guide us in all matters.’

The man left promptly to carry the message to all leaders of the rebellion, whatever their level of authority. They quickly grasped the aim of Mohammad Amin... so they set about following his advice. It seemed like no time at all when the wonderful painting was fixed to the wall of the first house on the main road leading into the district. It covered the wall entirely and was in full view of everyone entering the city. It was a picture that represented Holy Jerusalem and was so huge that it could be seen from far away.

The fateful time had come for the French military expedition to start moving into position to shell the entire district. The expedition proceeded with many military personnel of various ranks, and a vast amount of military impedimenta and heavy armaments, headed by one of the French commandants who had previously demonstrated great brutality in dealing with the people of Syria. He was fully determined to bomb the entire district on the pretext of attacking the terrorist rebels in their strongholds and hideouts.

As he approached the district he could not fail to see the enormous painting from afar. He was using his field-glasses to scan the land and prepare to give his orders to the tank crews and heavy-artillery soldiers to open fire... but what was that on the horizon? He called his adjutants and asked them to turn their field-glasses towards the entrance gate of the district, then he asked them, ‘Do you see what I see?’ Surely, a painting of Jerusalem was not what he expected to see!

They replied, ‘Yes... the people of this village must be Christians, without any doubt. So... the whole area must be Christian too... which means that most of its people are our brethren in religion... and they couldn’t possibly do what we have heard about them... we have no reason to destroy them. We have been given false information and whoever reported it must be punished.’

Their angry outbursts soon dissipated and the commander cooled down... he thought the best decision would be to withdraw and abandon all plans to shell the territory.

At once, he phoned the high commander of the French army in the government house and informed him of the situation; and the reply was simply, ‘So... it is a Christian area... the news which was reported to us by our spies was definitely wrong... retreat... let the people live in peace.’

The expedition leader replied, ‘Yes, sir... that’s my opinion too... we shall withdraw immediately.’

He quickly gave orders to the division to withdraw and return their terrible heavy armaments to the garrison.

By this action, Syria was saved from a dreadful fate which would surely have lead to its eventual destruction. Released from the terrible nightmare, the people returned to living in safety, peace, and tranquillity.

Yes... God had answered their prayers and saved them from grave danger and bloodshed: the loss of their crops which would have been burnt and scattered by the wind... the destruction of their houses which would have collapsed if fired on, burying the people inside.

The threat of wholesale slaughter was removed when Al’lah the Almighty inspired that true, obedient commando with His impressive Plan, for Mohammad Amin was always ready to suppress the evil and support the truth, his compatriots and his beloved homeland.

Our wise man employed extreme wisdom in his defence of the truth, and against the corruption of people’s hearts whilst cleverly concealing his behaviour from the French; his success came because he placed his trust in Al’lah to guide him in all his actions to support the rebels against France.

In fact, France suspected his duplicity but had no proof or evidence. Many times they tried to get rid of him, but Al’lah willed that he should fulfill his high aims in supporting the truth, and His merciful Providence intervened miraculously in every difficult situation to save him from certain death and preserve him from the cunning of France; for Al’lah is the Steering God and He would never humiliate someone who is truly obedient and faithful to Him.

So, with his sharp ingenuity, enlightened by Al’lah’s Light, Mohammad Amin was able to guide the people of this county with a ploy that ensured their safety and thereby spared them bloodshed and destruction.

Truly, it was the outcome of real communication with God, the fruit of Godly love, and a man’s unshakeable belief in Him.

chapters.title: Purer than the Whitest Snow
chapters.html:
Throughout the ages, shining stars and planets have turned consistently and unchanging within their orbits: forming part of this extremely accurate and perfectly regulated universe. Each one has its own specified purpose and function with which it supports all the others in order to accomplish its precise aim: flourishing life on earth.

The same Grand and Wise Management that brought this creation into being has also arranged for embryos to form in the wombs of their mothers and to allow new-born babies to see the light, for children to grow, the young and adults to live life to their fullest capacity: to be happy and share mutual love and intimacy with each other.

It is this very Omnipotence that drives the wind and clouds, provides the sun and drives it from one constellation to another, seizes the great asterisms, and moves the stars in their orbits.

What a grand, illustrious Authority it is that faultlessly controls and drives everything from the tiniest atoms wherever and whatever they may be, to the greatest galaxies, on earth as well as in the heavens: all leading to a perfectly planned outcome.

Here, we will quote the Prophetic saying to Ibn Abbas, the cousin of Al’lah’s Envoy, Mohammad (cpth), “Know for certain that had all the nations gathered to avail you they would be doing only what Al’lah had written for you; and had they helped each other to cause you harm, they would not succeed except within what Al’lah had written upon you [according to the bad deeds you had committed].”

Thus, Al’lah’s Hand of authority is spread constantly over the whole of creation and He is the Subduer Who overcomes His oppressive men according to the absolute fact that: there is no god but Al’lah, and this story gives confirmation of that fact.

We shall relate the story of a high-ranking officer (a major) in the government house of Damascus, whose envy and jealousy of a certain young officer increased day by day.

By virtue of his great aspiration and magnanimity, this young officer was called Aslan (the lion) since the Ottoman period, because of his outstanding bravery. His great efforts and successful deeds had led him to surpass his comrades even though they held higher rank than he did. So, the commander-in-chief of the army and the military, who also headed the security forces, placed great trust in him, as did the senior officers who treated this magnanimous officer with great cordiality and respect. They appreciated him for they acknowledged all of his deeds and brave actions, the like of which had never been matched by any other officer. This incited rage in the major, the subject of this story, whose superior rank in Damascus at that time as a supervisor for all departments of the gendarmerie in Damascus entitled him to make general, unannounced rounds of inspection whenever he pleased.

During this time, the honest officer, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, had recently been put in charge of al-Shaghour ﴿12﴾

police station, one of the security departments in Damascus. He was working diligently to be fully informed of its affairs: making an accurate and comprehensive assessment of every file and record to ensure that all was arranged as it should be; allocating his men to the security rounds, and generally ensuring order. All this was aimed at carrying out his work perfectly so that no fault could be found in any area...

Within a few days Mohammad Amin had almost accomplished his task of bringing faultless order to his department. However, he was soon to experience the jealousy of the major, as his inherent rancour would not permit him to live peacefully for he would definitely try to embitter other men’s lives as he himself was leading a disturbed life. He turned matters over in his mind, then realised that he should make an early inspection, indeed, within a few days, with the aim of finding fault with the new chief of the department; for the major sought to lessen our officer’s dignity in the heart of the commander-in-chief of the army and the other highranking officers. His malicious thoughts went so far as to hope that Mohammad Amin might have to face a court martial: he could have him removed from his position if he, the major, could uncover a lapse of sufficient severity.

With this aim in mind the major chose a day that was particular windy and snowy to go to the department for a sudden unannounced inspection... and we shall see that he certainly knew how to choose the most suitable day!!!

Unfortunately, Aslan’s preparations were still incomplete...!

And despite the violent snow storm, the inspector had left the government house and was making his way on horseback through the deep covering of snow which had created icy conditions underfoot and on the road.

He made his way steadily with his malicious intentions festering in his heart which was now also overcome by envy, and had turned so dark in contrast to the purity of the white snow which covered the earth in a splendid brilliance, attracting one’s thoughts to its Grand Provider.

What a poor man! How could he even see the glistening whiteness since his eyes had been veiled by a thick black screen of bitterness and malevolence? He slowly but surely steered his horse towards the target of his destructive thoughts as the snowflakes drifted gently from the heavens and covered the earth like a beautiful white blanket. But the heart of that envious man remained totally oblivious to the gifts that the Provider of the worlds had granted out of His Compassion and Love for all creatures!

The gentle snowflakes were sprinkling on his face yet he swept them away with his hand, angrily and nervously, sighing deeply. His hot, spiteful breaths ascended like small clouds and soon vanished in the frosty air.

Being on horseback he had no protection from the weather... he became so cold that he prodded the horse to hurry... leaving one road and turning on to another in a hurry to reach his destination.

In the security building, Aslan, the honourable officer, sat beside the stove near the window... in thoughtful mood he looked out at the perfect white snow that had covered the earth with its brilliant radiance... and sometimes turned his eyes to the sky from where the abundant snowflakes were falling. He felt the purity of the snow flowing into his heart so that he saw everything around him mingled with the brilliant white light and sensed great love for the Provider and Creator of the snow surging into his heart.

He remained there looking pensively through the window, feeling great fondness for the Obliger of gifts, the Rich One Who needs nothing from others and yet He grants lavish favours and great Benevolence.

Suddenly, Officer Aslan was disturbed by a dark form approaching through the whiteness of the snow! The horse was white and so were the rider’s clothes, yet the heart was dark!

Aslan recognised him: it was the general inspector for the police departments... and Aslan was well aware of the inspector’s intentions. What could be the reason for his visit at such a time and in stormy weather, if not to cause trouble?

The major dismounted and came in as he could feel the bitter cold creeping deeply into his bones.

The honourable officer, Mohammad Amin, was surprised by this unexpected arrival, particularly given the difficult weather conditions, and it was the first time he had experienced the strange impact of the hostility that had overwhelmed the man now standing before him.

The inspector-general sat on the chair by the table in the manager’s office. He asked, by name, for some specific folders which belonged to the section; Officer Aslan quickly brought them and placed them on the table. The major set about opening them, one after the other, scanning and searching carefully for any minor error that might enable him to charge the head of the police in the dock. But actually, how Great was Al’lah’s Care towards that honourable man! How would He allow anyone to hold sway over Aslan? On the contrary, His Will insisted on ennobling a true worshipper whose only aim had been to gain His Satisfaction.

So, as soon as that major opened the file he felt an intense shudder spreading throughout his limbs as though they were about to become detached from his body; suddenly, the folder fell from his hands and onto the table. Shaking and trembling he tumbled to the ground speechless! It was a severe attack brought about by foolishly travelling through the bitterly cold weather!

Astonished at the sudden collapse of the important inspector, our magnanimous officer Aslan immediately carried him to the next room where he laid him gently on the bed, removed his boots and wet jacket and covered him with blankets. He immediately lit the stove to heat the room and then turned back to him trying to ease the man’s suffering.

The glistening snow was still falling from the heavens and scattering generously across the earth, as far as the eye could see and indoors, the noble officer Aslan was fully occupied with the sick, spiteful man, offering him hot drinks and sparing no effort to care for him.

Truly, Mohammad Amin’s heart was as white as the snow, yet purer... its pure mercy was piling upon the heart of that malicious heart.

Night came and overwhelmed the place but in spite of its darkness, it seemed coloured with the purity of the white snow, while despite the late hour, the honourable master was still awake and attending to his bitter enemy.

His merciful heart did not allow him to leave the major alone for even a single moment and he continued to nurse him with the utmost care.

He burnt the midnight oil in order to soothe the man’s pains and offer him hot tisanes from time to time: what an amazing level of care which surpassed even that of a loving mother when she sympathises with her sick only son!

Indeed, if the level of compassion and tenderness shown to that malicious man had been poured upon a rocky mountain, the mountain would have been melted down by the sheer volume of love.

The patient was sleeping, and whenever he woke up he saw nothing but that honourable face above him, looking at him with eyes full of mercy and alive with compassion; and every time he averted his gaze because of his deep shame.

His heart became contrite and regretful because of his evil intention which had driven him to come. He felt a great sense of shame, disgrace and defeat before noble Aslan as he knew that if Aslan had cast him out he would have surely died in that snowstorm. Although Aslan was quite sure of the major’s cunning, malevolent intentions he did not respond to his evil... on the contrary, he responded by offering him floods of compassion and charity.

Actually, he forgave the major when he had been given the opportunity to retaliate which is a true characteristic of real men. He exemplified humanity in its fullest sense as he acted within Al’lah’s Satisfaction pursuant to the mercy, tenderness, and love he held for all mankind, whoever they were. Because of his pure, merciful heart which had never known rancour, malice or cruelty since it had been filled with love for his Provider, he treated the inspector as a helpless man whom he must willingly rescue. Our noble officer, Mohammad Amin, confronted the mistreatment with the best expressions of kindness even though the major had never offered Aslan any help whatsoever in the past.

He spent three days and nights serving and constantly watching him save for a few short naps. He did not go to his home at night or by day, even though the snow had stopped falling, until the patient began gradually to recover and the illness started to abate, along with the destructive disease of animosity and envy which had been supplanted by love for this humane man because of the outflowing of humanity enfolded within Mohammad Amin’s heart.

Thus, by such a magnificent, wise, humane action, Aslan was able to uproot the rancour and envy which might have ruined the major himself and others, due to a firm Godly rule. Since Officer Aslan is so honourable, straight and spotless, none can harm him as Al’lah protects, supports and aids him for his supreme humanity, and the flow of mercy stemming from his constantly resorting to Him, through which he derived mercifulness, sympathy, and tenderness: indeed all that exists of goodness, safety and tranquillity are ascribed to Al’lah, the Spring of all benevolence, compassion and kindness.

Having defied death with such merciful treatment, the inspector got up on the third day. He washed his face with hot water, combed his hair and smartened himself up, but he was still bound to his shame, wishing that the earth would open up and swallow him. He could not confront the honourable benefactor except with measureless thanks and extreme gratitude. However, he remained uneasy, wondering, ‘Is there still such a man on earth? Can it be that there are some hearts whiter and more abundant than the snow from the heavens?’

Never had he thought that he would find a man like that officer whose heart possessed such a high level of clarity and purity. That is why he became increasingly ashamed of himself and disdained his own bad characteristics which were inciting him to evil.

The major left the department cloaked in his own disgrace but he made a promise to himself to change his conduct after he sensed the clarity flowing into his heart out of the assiduity of Aslan, the merciful officer.

As the days... months... and years passed, noble Aslan achieved shinig success, bringing him both pride and glory and which perpetuated him in the memories of people at that time. It further promoted his dignity with his leaders, until it pleased the Almighty God to ensure his appointment to the prestigious position of governor of Damascus Castle, and its jail which brought considerable prestige and was aspired to by all the ranking officers.

The first thing he did when he entered his office as general manager of the castle was to lock the door and behind it prostrate himself before his Provider, thanking and praising Him for what he had been granted. He was so grateful that Al’lah Almighty had predestined that he would enter the jail as an influential officer, not as a humble prisoner, as a master, not a criminal, and as a governor, not a convict.

He started his reformative works in the castle, thanking Al’lah for His Gifts.

However, one must keep in mind that there were enraged hearts fraught with animosity and filled with envy, for they wondered why Aslan, the Arab officer, had been appointed to that prestigious position, thinking themselves more worthy of it. They forgot that they had never performed any outstanding deed that might resemble his, nor had they approached his level of humane sacrifice through which he released people from the grave danger and evils of the outlaws and criminals for whom he was always lying in wait.

Indeed, they neglected to tell that he used to readily storm the perils endangering his soul, fearing none of those bands whom he confronted at Mount Qasiyun, ﴿13﴾

the Kurdish area, exposing himself to death again and again in order to dispel evil and enjoin goodness.

Because of their wicked intentions, those envious men began to watch him and trace every act and movement he made inside the castle. They were determined to find fault with him through which he might be accused and condemned so that his prestige would decline and so would his dignity, consequently, they hope he would be dismissed from his position at the castle.

This was their malicious intention and they began to wait for the right moment with eyes filled with evil and wicked malice.

At that time, there were a lot of defective things in the castle which needed to be put to rights: there was a lack of basic stationery, and the officers’ office furniture needed to be replaced.

Officer Mohammad Amin took all that into account and put his plan into effect. Then, he looked at other parts of the castle: there were unused, forgotten areas in which he found large wooden poles used for supporting the electricity wires. They had been discarded and were only fit to be burnt for heating.

He thought of their position and reached a decision when the gendarmes told him that they needed many instruments and sets of stationery, and that they had a lot of items that had been discarded because they had been damaged by being exposed to unfavourable weather conditions; therefore they were of no further use either. It would be, therefore, advantageous to sell them and buy the necessary stationery with the money received, so, they would be autonomous and not need to charge the cost to the treasury.

That was the request of his men so, he agreed and told them to sell the poles as wood for heating and to sell other discarded items and use the money received to buy the necessary stationery for the castle’s needs.; for it was his firm belief that the government money should be spent primarily on serving the state and its citizens.

Accordingly, on the following day, the sale of the spoiled poles was effected and the necessary stationery was purchased It did not occur to him that this straightforward management decision might rebound on him. Yet the evil eyes of those hateful, envious people were still noting his every action, so they waited until the poles were sold and then they presented a report to the inspectorate charging Officer Mohammad Amin Sheikho with stealing the state’s possessions for his own benefit.

The report reached the appropriate authority who issued a decision which entailed the formation of a full committee to go to the castle on a specific date in order to investigate the contents of the report and its credibility.

Officer Aslan was informed and he retorted, ‘What! Am I charged with stealing the state’s possessions! Is that really what is stated in the report?’

‘Yes... it’s true, and they have appointed a committee to come to the castle and investigate the matter.’

‘No... no, that’s not reasonable. How silly to do that... for these useless poles which had been left in the open would definitely be wasted if I hadn’t sold them to the advantage of the castle! Actually, I did that only to dispose of them and make use of the money for the benefit of the castle. By God! I did not think for a moment that I may be indicted for such negligible things! So this is the plan and the aim of those slanderers...!’

He was really saddened and surprised by that news, so he went out to ask some of his acquaintances who had expert knowledge on such subjects and their implications. Unfortunately, he found that he would definitely be charged since the sale had not been authorised by the lawful agreement of the authority, nor had the items been disposed of through a public auction which would have required a lot of special arrangements to be taken in advance. However, this had not been mentioned by his men (the gendarmes) who were not fully aware of the law, so.... what would he do?

It was a real problem for which he had to find a solution as soon as possible.

Feeling dejected and extremely confused, he left his comrades and went for a walk in the street... his mind fully occupied with many questions.

Amidst the officer’s deep sadness and bewilderment it pleased Al’lah Almighty to lead him to meet the major who had been manager of the inspection unit which supervised the sections. And he was the very officer whose evil intentions noble Aslan had confronted with great charity and overflowing tenderness and mercy that issued from his noble heart. This officer was the same major whom Aslan had saved from certain death; the major had never forgotten, even for a single day, his magnificent favour, splendid care, and great humane treatment. And he thought often of the white snow, that is, the bounty of Aslan’s heart which is alive with sympathy, humanness, and charity derived from his Provider.

At the moment he met him, he greeted him cheerfully, ‘How are you dear Aslan? I’ve missed you so much, tell me, how are you?’

Aslan replied, ‘Thanks to your presence, major... I’m fine.’

He gazed at Aslan’s face, then he said, ‘But you seem distressed and uneasy! Tell me... what’s the matter?’

‘No... no, nothing.’

‘Surely not! This is not your nature. By God, tell me about your problem... maybe I’ll be able to help you!’

Aslan began to relate his story to the major, and when he had heard every last detail, he said, ‘Did they really accuse you? No, no, that’s wrong... you’re honest, pure and merciful, even though they have schemed against you. What villains!’ Then he smiled and said, ‘But would such a silly thing as this upset you my upright officer?’

‘Why not? Since this plot and their malice is strong enough to wreck a mountain!’

‘No, my friend! You are righteous, pure-hearted and loyal to your home... the matter is not nearly as serious as you think as I am the supervisor of the general depositories of the county now.’

The major asked Aslan for a sheet of paper, took out his pen and wrote, ‘I declare that I have received all of the used poles and transported them to my depositories.’ Then he backdated the paper, signed it and handed it to Aslan.

Thus, it pleased Al’lah Almighty to rescue that faithful man from this ordeal and remove the hold that others had over him, because he was a lofty, supreme, humane man in the highest sense of these words.

Indeed! God sent him that officer at the right moment so that he might repay a small part of Aslan’s great favour towards him.

On the appointed date, and within official hours, the commission arrived to begin their enquiries.

The malevolent enviers came too... they were so eager to see Aslan accused in the court and face a prison sentence, and they were certain that this day would be decisive in their doing away with Officer Aslan and determine his end.

The commission and some malicious slanderers were still in the deserted area of the castle where the spoiled poles had been stored. They summoned Aslan who stepped out of his office feeling safe and tranquil, and immediately he presented the paper which demonstrated that he was aware of the false accusations made against him: it was a legal and impeccable letter of receipt issued by the general manager of the public depositories, and stated that all of the items in dispute had been received at the official depositories.

So, Aslan was proven to be as honest and faultless as ever and he was surely innocent of everything written against him. His accusers, on the other hand, would now have to answer for their false reports and their attempts to defame his honesty.

Having viewed Aslan’s letter and understood the contents, the slanderers were severely shocked and could not believe what they had seen with their own eyes. They were even more shocked when they were informed of the decision of the formal commission that they would have to answer officially for their malicious actions. They were indeed thunderstruck and confused at how suddenly their scheming had been turned against them..

Truly, evil schemes will always entrap their perpetrators!

Thus we learn, dear reader, that performing charitable acts safeguards against bad ends, since the rule of justice prevails over all of creation, for Al’lah’s Hand is predominant over all, and everyone receives their rights and dues. So, know for certain that if everyone in the nation gathered to harm you, they would never succeed unless you have committed a bad deed yourself and it was written against you by Al’lah.

Stabilise goodness in yourself by your own deeds and actions, and then none shall hold any sway over you.

chapters.title: The Conspiracy against the Head of the Citadel
chapters.html:
In this account we speak of the exceptional attributes of Mohammad Amin Sheikho: his outstanding bravery, and his exceptional powers of thought and beneficence. He shone with the warmth of true faith, his body was strong and vital in its movements, his every step was steady and firm, and his powerful voice echoed from the hills. The gleam of determination intermingled with waves of mercy shone from his eyes. His face was radiant and, in its reverence, appeared like a wonderful, brilliant sun suspended high in the sky its light reflecting on and inspiring his men. The reality was that as the moon controls the tides of the oceans, so he controlled and brought harmony to all around him.

His process of thought never ceased to dissect and analyse all problems; his firm heart, steadfast spirit, intensive plans for fighting, and his unprecedented genius for combative tactics ensured that he destroyed the criminals’ power and turned them – if they did not repent – into muddy pools emptied of their foul, stagnant water.

Truly, he was like the lion king in terms of bravery. Indeed, he deserved to have been a commander of those renowned Islamic battles of the past: those victories and conquests that rendered eternal Arabic Islamic glory to the Caliph and all Muslims wherever they may be.

The many practical trials to which he was subjected revealed his renowned innate essence to the extent that the French leaders themselves had no choice but to rely on him in their security plans even though he was an Arab officer. And why not employ an Arab officer, since he could work miracles when it came to establishing the truth, eliminating injustice and oppression, and spreading safety and security among the citizens? And so it should be, even if the country was under French administration.

Yes, indeed, he provoked admiration by his bravery based on his true belief in God, the One, the Almighty, and God was Sufficient for him. He drew near to Him because of his unique genius and unparalleled courage which made him great among his peers so that all of them held him in the highest esteem, to the extent that some of them would even kiss his boots.

As for those men whose hearts had been blinded because of their pride and aberration, they swore by all that was evil to turn people away from the straight path and cast their evilminded insinuations on the Prophet’s wishes, that prevented people from finding the right way, the way of escape, and ultimately would drive them to commit forbidden acts.

They bore all the debased qualities whether they knew it or not. This was obvious when they faced him or even thought about him, which caused them to flare up with rage. They were extremely envious of this officer because of the high degrees, great honours and commendations that he had attained by his devotion to all that was true, therefore they continuously lied and conspired against him. These actions of theirs failed to harm him and, indeed, caused misfortune only for those who truly deserved it. They had no power over him as he was close to Al’lah, and remained ever faithful in his love for Him; so the Almighty supported and protected him.

He devoted himself wholeheartedly and sacrificed his life for the sake of pleasing God by doing good to all His creatures, therefore no other man could be compared with him. He did not achieve such a high rank by cheating, lying or deception, yet he paid its price a hundred-fold: how many times did he face death for the sake of supporting the truth and ensuring that all people could enjoy safety and peace surrounded by good fortune.

The Compassionate God leaves no man with unfulfilled desires in this earthly life if he has deserved it. And anyone that is true in his requests will have them granted according to his truthfulness and honesty, and so will be responsible for his own choices in life.

This noble man held the post of director of the Damascus Citadel during the French Mandate: an extremely important position which all the officers aspired to and competed for. Due to his uncontrollable envy, one of these officers eventually managed to persuade the military leaders that Officer Mohammad Amin was not qualified for this post by providing apparent evidence of many false claims against him. Of course, his malicious cronies supported one another so that they managed to convince the Minister of the Interior of Officer Sheikho’s unsuitability for this position and order his unjustified dismissal and discharge from the entire military service.

One morning, he was taken aback when he entered his office to find the replacement director handing him his discharge papers, with an obvious smile on his face which expressed his fiendish joy at our officer’s misfortune.

This decision held no surprise for Mohammad Amin, and losing this post caused him no grief at all as he had undergone far worse situations in his life, and even faced death many times. So, this news given to him by such a fiend did not cause any grudge to enter into his heart: a heart that had been filled with Godly Light.

Without uttering a word, Officer Mohammad Amin took the immediate decision to leave the office, then slowly and calmly walked across the courtyard of the citadel heading for his horse, completely absorbed in his thoughts.

He knew full well that it was a conspiracy at the hands of one of the other officers who envied him for his success, so he did not care about it for his own sake, but he considered its effects on the security of the people. This post was no more than a means for him to do good deeds by which he sought his Provider’s Satisfaction, and if his dismissal meant that this path was no longer open to him he would find many alternative means as long as he had the ability to think.

He mounted his horse and spurred it on, then trotted briskly until he left the citadel behind.

That was God’s Will, and it is sufficient for man to be given such lessons in this life in order to believe that there is no god but Al’lah.

Mohammad Amin surrendered to Al’lah wholeheartedly, seeking strength, assistance and guidance from Him: for Al’lah alone is the Steering God and the Provider of aid.

The Godly Fates willed that every man should be allowed his own freedom of choice if he was sincere in his request, and even though those envious accusers had sought to satisfy the evil trends settled in their hearts, and to enjoy the outward brilliance of this worldly life, their request was also granted.

After Officer Mohammad Amin had left the citadel, the new officer immediately assumed his position and set about laughing and joking with all those around him. He did not know how to fill his time... should he drink coffee or smoke a narghile ﴿14﴾

...? He thought about all the good things (as he thought!) that this position would bring for him. His friends would come the following day to congratulate him and he would turn up his nose at all the others, and give senseless, frivolous orders to the soldiers who would be like slaves for him. One thing is certain: he was not fulfilling his duties as the director of the citadel!

He would take bribes to increase his wealth, keep at bay those who disapproved of his behaviour, while taking those who were unprincipled and corrupt to be his cronies.

This is God’s Will, for He is not questioned about His Actions.

Mohammad Amin went back home, took off his military uniform, put on his casual clothes and placed a white hat on his head so that he looked like a tall, handsome, venerable man. And as was the habit of the people of Damascus in the warm months of spring and summer, in the afternoon he sat on his carved wooden chair in the street, in front of his house, holding Al’lah’s Book in his hands, reciting its verses in a calm, steady voice with a sober heart, and giving time to deep contemplation; this is where he would stay until sunset. This became his idyllic routine and he would spend his days in this manner, as if he were on a trip to the shores of a great sea with tall shady trees surrounding him and the sun rising and setting in all its splendour. His heart was at ease as he drank in the endless joys of being close to God.

However, as will be seen, his dismissal could not come into effect unless God willed it. It was on just such a divinely-inspired day, while he was studying the Holy Qur’an, that a large delegation of high-ranking and eminent people arrived: they stood before him and greeted him formally.

He raised his head to see the Minister of the Interior and the Chief of Police accompanied by a crowd of senior military officers. He closed the Qur’an and kissed it, then he stood up to receive them one by one as they shook hands with him and kissed him, as was the custom. Mohammad Amin greeted them as welcome guests and received them hospitably in his home.

The meeting began with an air of silent tranquillity that lay over the shady courtyard. They all bowed their heads but every one of them was smiling optimistically. The Minister of the Interior started to address Mohammad Amin with distinguished, solemn words which ran off his tongue, revering and glorifying the man before him. The minister did not know quite what to say... in fact he was relating Mohammad Amin’s honourable deeds, one after the other, in his desire to express the high opinion they held of this officer – head of the citadel. And all those eminent officials gathered there joined the minister in praising him, and declared that they had made a gross error of judgement when they had believed the denunciation of that liar and dismissed Officer Mohammad Amin from his post. Then they begged him – despite their lofty positions – to return to his office and they apologised profusely for underestimating him in this serious matter.

Mohammad Amin was astonished at this complete about face and answered them, ‘But, as I was dismissed nineteen days ago, according to the law, I have the right to refuse to return to work; is that not so?’’

They replied, ‘Yes, you are right. But we have come to you hoping that you will accept our request. As for those days, we shall consider them as working days. So would you please accept our request? There and then he answered, ‘If this is what you truly want I will comply with pleasure.

They were extremely happy to have succeeded in such a delicate mission. But as for Mohammad Amin and his eldest son, they were amazed at these goings-on, for what had led to the reversal of opinion that would have him reinstated? He was a patient man and tomorrow would come soon enough. For as most people surely know: patience is a virtue.

The following day he discovered the reason behind their request. In fact unknown to our officer, there had been a serious event that shook the very foundations of the whole nation to the extent that people still remember it till the present time. During the Arabic officer’s absence from the citadel, the hardened criminals who had been sentenced to death or to life imprisonment managed to escape from the citadel after digging a tunnel that started from their cell in the prison and stretched eastwards to end in a shop in al- Asronia market.

They dug the tunnel and sneaked into the shop, then they impatiently waited for its owner. When he opened it as usual in the morning he was most surprised to find a number of hefty men who threw him to the ground and quickly ran off to disappear in the warren of narrow lanes. There were sixteen prisoners in all and every one of them managed to escape and remain hidden.

All of that happened during the time when the officer who had replaced Mohammad Amin by plotting and scheming still held his post. Did he not hold this post at his own request? Was this not what he wanted? The reader should note that the course of three different matters came together by God’s Will:

The first was the will of the French government that turned against this humane officer without any evidence against him.

The second was the illegal efforts of the accuser to be appointed to this post by his dishonourable attitude, his heart full of hatred, and false accusations.

The third was the escape of the prisoners from their cell thereby avoiding their sentences of execution or lifeimprisonment.

God’s good Steering willed that our scholar, that noble officer, should be uplifted in order to add to his eminence, and to avoid him suffering the shame or disgrace of his glorious illustrious life history being stained with failure or loss.

In the same way that His Steering willed that this covetous man should fulfill his wishes illegally, and then for him to be punished severely and taste failure and humiliation after giving way to his desires, and to be burned with the fire of regret afterwards.

This sudden, unexpected surprise was like a bolt from the blue that struck him so forcibly that it seemed to toss him like a feather in a whirlwind. Insults were heaped upon him by his superiors in front of his soldiers, and his shortlived position of power was lost forever, his arrogance and contempt disappearing like a puff of smoke.

If he had not been so fond of this worldly life and its pleasures he would have held a pistol to his head and fired, or he would have tied his own feet and attached them to the hooves of a horse to be dragged in the dust of failure to a desolate place where he would live out a solitary existence in a small room.

As for the citadel, it had become a dark and sombre place without the presence of its illustrious director who resembled the brilliance of the full moon and the shining sun. Every stone of its walls longed for the return of the light to shine and reflect the brilliant hues of the victorious Arab prestige, and then to add to its glories and forget the shady, gloomy past caused by callous, unmerciful people.

Thus, Officer Mohammad Amin returned to the citadel as an even higher and more praiseworthy master, and Al’lah saved him as He willed: “They plot and plan, but Al’lah plans too.” ﴿15﴾

The summary:

This is the Will of Al’lah, the Wise, the Just. Those who had been sentenced to death managed to dig a tunnel under the fence of the citadel and flee to al-Asronia market which was situated close behind it. Al’lah had prevented their escape during the tenure of Officer Mohammad Amin, then when the envious man schemed against him the disaster occurred under the management of those who had plotted against Mohammad Amin. And after the success of this conspiracy for his dismissal, the disaster eventually fell upon the one who had plotted the evil deed, and so it returned to him: “The plotting of evil will hem in only those who instigate it.” ﴿16﴾

chapters.title: Persistence in Prayer Leads to Enlightenment
chapters.html:
One day Mohammad Amin Sheikho was present at an assembly, which was being addressed by his sheikh, where he heard certain words that caused his pure heart to be overcome with rage that penetrated to the depths of his spirit.

The sheikh said, ‘Oh, man! If your prayers do not lead you to understand the Almighty’s Words and to realise the meaning of the Quranic verses which you recite during your prayers it would not be true communication with God: no... it would not be meaningful prayer but, rather, an empty gesture for the Prophet (cpth) said, “A man attains nothing from prayer except what is implanted in his mind.”

These words disturbed him and caused him to toss and turn throughout the ensuing sleepless night as they began to invade the very depths of his spirit, ‘Oh, my Provider! I am extremely distressed,’ he thought. ‘I pray for communication with You yet I find that my thoughts and my spirit wander and invariably go to thinking about criminals in their hideouts, and the crimes they have committed... I am constantly devising schemes to capture them and bring them to justice; and when I finish my prayers I go off to carry out the plans and schemes which I thought up while I should have been concentrating on my prayers.

‘Then, the deeds I have carried out and the sacrifices which I have made with the aim of gaining Al’lah’s Satisfaction have not led me to the proper communication with Al’lah because I still have not truly understood the teaching contained in His Words, nor have I recognised these precious pearls of wisdom given from the Highest Treasure through His Love. Since my prayer has failed to lead me to that deeper understanding it must, therefore, be flawed, and I’m mistaken in my understanding of His Words. So my communication is nothing but an automatic motion through which I seek solutions for my own problems and schemes to pursue criminals and eradicate criminality.

‘This means, quite simply, that I have not attained the full realisation of the supreme meaning of Al’lah’s Words, that is, the Holy Qur’an.

‘Oh, my Provider! What should I do? I’m sure my destiny will be to join the dwellers of Hell! Since any man who has abandoned his communication with Al’lah has not one iota of goodness in his spirit!’

Through such internal spiritual discussions he became overwhelmed by a desperate state of sadness which led to a bout of heart-rending weeping. But eventually he dried his tears and went to his sheikh to bid him goodnight in his customary polite and dignified fashion. This was two hours after the evening prayer, when the city was calm as its inhabitants were sleeping soundly in their beds.

On the way home, the same melancholy thoughts returned to oppress him again, and once more he was moved to tears and sighed deeply. The closer he got to his home the more disconsolate he became, and he thought, ‘Am I right to feel that I really don’t communicate with Al’lah? And if so, will I go to Hell?’ Waves of sorrow and grief overwhelmed his pure heart, and his virtuous eyes shed tears expressing his remorse and pain for fear of what his ultimate fate might be... till eventually he reached the electricity poles along the foot of the mountain on the road leading to his home. Here a bitter spiritual state overwhelmed him so he stopped and leant against one of the poles and began to weep bitterly, ‘Don’t I pray in the appropriate way? Am I really destined for Hell?’

He was still in that pitiable state when he arrived home, where he stood by the door leaning against a pole with his virtuous tears flowing copiously, and obsessed by a single thought that festered in his mind. Again and again, the same question went around inside his head, ‘Will I go to Hell? Is it true that I really do not pray as a man should?’

Then he went into his room and closed the door; yet his emotional state was rapidly deteriorating to the point where he became utterly exhausted from crying and bewailing his fate, and finally he was overcome by mental exhaustion and fell asleep. He got up when the call to prayer issued from the minarets and woke him from his fitful sleep.

He rushed off to respond to the call of his Provider as he always did, and went to perform the ritual ablutions at the fountain in the courtyard; his tears began to flow once more down his cheeks and fall to mingle with the water of the fountain!

His feelings of despair overwhelmed him most forcefully once again, ‘Shall I be destroyed? Shall I end up in Hell... because my communication with Al’lah is not from the heart... it’s merely a movement of the lips? I say the words but my thoughts wander away from the Words of my Great God... this is not right... His tormented spirit asked him, ‘Why do you pray since you do not communicate with God during your prayer?’ The answer came to him, ‘If you do not communicate with God during your prayer should you not keep on praying so that you may one day attain this communication?’

Tears continued to cloud his eyes and trickle down his cheeks, his deepening sorrow and obvious distress etched clearly on his face. He stayed a long time at the fountain washing away his tears but no sooner had he dried his face than his tears were shed anew.

How could it be otherwise when he believed that he was not communicating with Al’lah as he felt that he should, and that whoever foundered in his prayer to Al’lah would surely be destined for the flames of Hell!

He stayed there, his spirit completely preoccupied by these thoughts, till it became quite late. He looked around him at the courtyard and found that he had missed the communal prayer by being so overwhelmed by his own personal suffering and the waves of sorrow and grief that continued to wash over him. He then decided to pray in his room and having entered he turned to Kiblah ﴿17﴾

to perform the dawn prayer.

But, no sooner had he begun, by proclaiming that Al’lah is Greater, and started to recite the Opening fortress of the Holy Qur’an, “In the Name of God, the All-Compassionate, the All-Merciful”, than he saw a luminous apparition crowned with the Godly Light and Divine Brilliance. The spectre addressed him saying, ‘Praise is to God my brother!’

At this, our merciful man began to pay attention to the words of this radiant person who was undoubtedly Al’lah’s Envoy (cpth). Indeed, through this communication Mohammad Amin became overwhelmed by this Godly Manifestation and the most brilliant sanctified lights. He felt that he was ascending the ranks of perfection from one level to the next, and was now able to fully understand the meanings of the verses of the Opening fortress, one by one. It was as though the heaviest weight had been lifted from his shoulders, and a feeling of sublime happiness seemed to spread throughout his body: his spirit flew throughout the universe, viewing and soaring above all of its creatures. The more that he witnessed the Supreme Attributes of God manifested in His Creation, the more his love for Him grew, and the more feelings of sublime happiness he enjoyed. Indeed, his spirit rose to the highest and most sacred realms of God’s Kingdom.

Truly, he attained the proper communication after giving himself wholeheartedly to pursuing the correct path. That resplendent man, the Envoy (cpth), had recited the Opening fortress to Mohammad Amin and continued to recite these Holy Words till he came to, “Guide us to the straight path.”

And here, Mohammad Amin had a sudden sense of enlightenment as the rays of the noonday sun shone over his noble countenance, blinding him with its brilliance as it shone through the window and fell upon him in his room. Thereupon, he quickly completed his prayers in a continued state of extreme elation and feelings of a great closeness to God. His prayers over he rushed out to the courtyard to be sure that it was, in fact, noon. He found that the sun had reached its zenith! Many hours had passed while he was lost deep in contemplation and prayer, though in fact he felt as if it were but a few minutes. No wonder! For how should he feel since he was rapturous at his ascent ever higher up the ladder of supreme perfection. He was entirely immersed in viewing the most beautiful heavenly sights through his heart-eye and hearing the sweet Tone of Al’lah, his most beloved One (Glory to Him), addressing him through His Envoy (cpth). Thus, during this sacred communication with God Mohammad Amin had achieved the Godly Perfections, both mentally and spiritually, and derived absolute perfection from the Source of the Godly Presence and the only Absolute, Perfect God, that is Al’lah, the Almighty.

So, from this, one understands that the Almighty’s Benevolence is boundless and He grants it to those who truly wish for it, for Al’lah is the Greatest Benefactor.

chapters.title: Morality Is Maintained
chapters.html:
The events related in this story occurred during the 1940s at the end of the French Mandate over Syria.

It began when a member of the al-Maleh family married a daughter of a good-hearted sheikh who lived in the same quarter as the eminent scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho. This man held the rank of colonel in the military, and without any doubt, this was regarded as a considerable worldly position at that time; furthermore, the colonel owned a car, which was extremely rare during that era and normally only a dream to be aspired to.

After the young wife went to live at her husband’s home he began to annoy her by asking her to sit with his comrades, the French officers, even though she had never been accustomed to doing such a thing for she had received a virtuous Islamic upbringing and had been raised to a high moral standard. Her firm principles and strong character led her to disdain all casual mixing between men and women. Furthermore, she totally rejected the unveiling of women in the presence of strange men, for she knew intuitively that it displeases Al’lah Almighty.

Thus, in due course the chasm between the man and his wife became very wide and their quarrels intensified, as each of them was looking at life from a completely different perspective.

The wife remained patient until she could no longer bear the reality of her new life, and the matter reached a climax. Without a word to her husband, she put on her wrap and, perfectly veiled, she left her husband’s house. She had decided to sacrifice his high rank and worldly prestige, caring nothing for the life of luxury she was leaving behind. Nor did she give a thought to all the difficulties and inconveniences that her husband, the colonel, might cause as a reaction to her deserting the marital home. It is a fact that these things were of no importance to her for she cared only about gaining Al’lah’s Satisfaction and adhering to her faith.

And so, she arrived unexpectedly at her father’s house and appealed to him not to make her return to her husband. She explained the impossible situation she had been forced to endure and told him that she would never go back.

Her kindly father, the sheikh, realised the extent of her suffering and set about sending his representatives to convince the colonel of the necessity of divorcing his daughter. He realised that she did not belong in the colonel’s environment and would never become accustomed to the social lifestyle associated with his rank however long they might stay together. On the contrary, their staying together would only cause the disagreements to increase and their life would become like hell for both of them.

In spite of all the attempts aimed at convincing him to divorce her, the arrogant colonel did not listen to anyone and refused to give in to their demands.

People advised her father to seek the help of the noble master who happened to live in the very same street. They advised the sheikh that the only one who could solve his problem was Mohammad Amin and that he should resort to no one else for assistance.

But, for unknown reasons, this sheikh was not well disposed towards Mohammad Amin. Perhaps because they held differing points of view on certain matters, or possibly because they belonged to the circles of different sheikhs: but surely this is the attitude only of narrow-minded people, and completely neglects the concept of brotherhood among Muslims. In fact, this is exactly what had prevented him from discussing his problem with Mohammad Amin.

Thus, because of his stubborn pride he continued to ask for the help and advice of his acquaintances, and to send many influential residents from his district to intercede with the colonel, his son-in-law, hoping that they might convince him to divorce his daughter. However, every time the efforts of the sad father failed and he could say nothing but ‘There is no might nor power except by Al’lah’, ascribing the situation to Al’lah’s Fate just like all those neglectful people who attribute every personal fault to destiny.

When he realised that he was unable to resolve the situation satisfactorily, he responded to the wise, well-meaning advice of his neighbours and the people around him who told him that, ‘There is only one man who can help you to settle this problem... Mohammad Amin (Abu Fathi)... he’s the only one who can convince the colonel to divorce your daughter.’

Driven by the sad sighs and whimpers of both his daughter and his wife, the sheikh was forced to approach Mohammad Amin to relate his story in detail. He described the colonel’s obstinacy and the unhappiness of his daughter, her concerns about her religion and honour, and her wish to be divorced from that detestable man. He said that he would like the scholar’s help to solve his daughter’s problem with the man who had great prestige and held a high official position.

After hearing the full details of the case and of how the colonel had behaved extremely badly in wronging the sheikh’s poor daughter, the venerable scholar reassured the sheikh, as he was accustomed to do with all those who sought his assistance. He was able to do this because of the wisdom which was granted to him by Almighty Al’lah, whereby he always diagnosed the disease and prescribed the fitting remedy. So, he soothed and eased the grief of the poor father saying, ‘I’ll come to visit you tomorrow evening and your son-in-law (the colonel) will come too. He will not refuse my request and the problem will be solved by Al’lah’s Permission. So, stop worrying, trust in Almighty Al’lah, and consider the problem resolved.’

It so happened that a brother of the colonel in our story was a disciple of the scholar, Mohammad Amin. This brother was in the habit of always attending the lectures of his revered guide. So, our noble scholar asked him to accompany the colonel to the house of his father-in-law where he, Mohammad Amin, would wait for him. Needless to say, the colonel’s brother responded readily, feeling more than happy to offer assistance to another human being.

At the agreed time, the noble master went to the sheikh’s house, then the colonel, wearing his perfect regimental uniform, arrived by car.

Since people generally consider that such a man has considerable prestige and holds a distinguished rank, he entered the house his head held high to show his pride in his worldly position. He sat near to scholar Mohammad Amin who began talking to him about the conflict existing between him and his wife, endeavouring to convince him in a gentle and amicable way. But alas! He had misconstrued the situation and considered that progress and civilisation would be advanced through social intercourse between men and women: in which case there was nothing wrong in his wife mixing with men, being broad-minded, and having her own opinion in conversation and other matters!

This was the colonel’s firm point of view and he viewed everything according to his own entrenched ideas which he deeply admired; consequently, the logical speech of the noble master had no effect on him as he was determined to adhere to his own opinions!

The eminent master, Mohammad Amin, addressed him saying, ‘But, why do you conceal this contrariness in yourself? Don’t you claim that you seek advancement and civilisation?’

The colonel said, ‘Of course! This is how I always conduct myself and it is not merely a claim!’

Scholar Mohammad Amin said, ‘So, doesn’t advancement and civilisation entail that every human being should have his own freedom of choice?’

‘Yes.’ replied the colonel, without any hesitation whatsoever.

The venerable scholar then asked, ‘So why do you force your wife to do what she doesn’t like? Why do you ask her to change her morals and her manners, and to act against the Islamic laws with which she conforms in order to achieve Al’lah’s Satisfaction?’

The colonel remained silent, so Mohammad Amin continued, ‘And then, when she asks for separation as a result of your pressuring her to follow your ways and adopt your principles (although even Al’lah Almighty has never compelled any creature) you repeatedly refuse her request?’

Thus the colonel was eventually convinced by the logic of the scholar’s words, and deeming himself to be above being considered incompatible with his own principles he said, ‘If she comes here now and says to me, “I don’t want you”, I shall divorce her at once!’

Until that moment, he still thought that she wanted him as she would never find a man with such prestige and high reputation to replace him. He assumed that it was her family, and not her, behind her demand and that the matter had been merely one of complaining and grumbling after which she would inevitably calm down and return to his home. He was certain that she would never give him up as long as he held that high rank, wide prestige, and great fortune.

The noble master then addressed the sheikh saying, ‘Would you tell your daughter to put on her veil and come here in order to do as her husband has asked?’

The poor sheikh said, ‘But, we are afraid of him... yes, I’m afraid of him... oh, Bey, ﴿18﴾

please!’

Frustrated at the sheikh’s reaction Mohammad Amin shouted at him, ‘Hurry up... go and call your daughter!’ At that moment the old man could do nothing but comply with our master, and rushed off to carry out his order.

When the chaste woman arrived at the door dressed in black and completely veiled from the top of her head to the bottom of her feet, the venerable scholar addressed her saying, ‘Listen to me my daughter, and carefully consider your response, for the decision will be final and irrevocable.

You stand before your husband now and you have his full attention, so if you want him and wish to stay with him, we shall bring about a reconciliation between you both since there is a solution for every problem. However, if you don’t want to stay in his house and don’t want him as your husband, we’ll bring about an official separation because this is not an acceptable situation for a spouse’s lifetime. It rests with you to decide now... if you still want him say, “Yes”, but if you don’t, say, “No”!’

Without hesitation the woman replied, ‘No!’

The word struck the heart of the colonel as a resounding shock, as his arrogance would not let him accept that response... her refusal came as an extreme affront to him, to the extent that he felt himself to be like a flimsy straw spinning in a vast space. The shock caused him to become pale and dizzy, and unable to look at those in attendance, since he thought that he had been completely degraded in their eyes, and would be, thereafter, in the view of all of society.

He turned towards the modest woman and said, ‘My wife is divorced... divorced... divorced; thus I have divorced her three times, and this cannot be rescinded.’ With this statement the colonel fully and finally renounced his wife, and the divorce was witnessed by the venerable scholar and the colonel’s brother.

Hence, the distress of this poor family was cast aside and this virtuous woman felt as if she were a bird which had been liberated from the confines of its oppressive cage.

As for her father, the sheikh, he became convinced of all that he had heard about this wise, humane master, and ashamed of his own negative thoughts towards him; these thoughts were instantly replaced with those of his fullest admiration and great appreciation. He did not know how to reward or thank him for his great favour, so he asked Al’lah Almighty to recompense him with whatever he deserved.

The colonel left the sheikh’s house, never to return, whereas the Almighty Al’lah compensated that virtuous woman with a husband as good and pure as her with whom to spend the rest of her life, according to her sound character and adherence to perfect Godly Law.

chapters.title: Timely Repayment of a Debt
chapters.html:
Once one has departed this lower life, it becomes merely a series of reminiscences, and nothing more... a temporary period of diligence, like a dream, interrupted by death. Oh... you lower life! Your attractive lustre repeatedly lures the eyes of those who fail to pay attention to Him Who created you and gifted you with all these earthly pleasures! A limited time of inadvertence... then, the sight will sharpen and this fascinating life will be stripped of its ornaments and its reality will be uncovered.

You will realise that it has been no more than a mirage, while Al’lah Almighty is the Truth. The purpose in coming here has never been for the enjoyment of this worldly life, indeed it is for us to reach out and communicate with its Creator Who has supplied it with all that it holds, and to amass sublime deeds with which He pleases. In this way, we draw nearer to Him and rise to approach His Presence.

It is a fact that both the one who commits evil deeds and the one who is charitable and mindful of Al’lah will ultimately depart this lower earthly life... but there is a great difference between them: the first will suffer a horrible, sorrowful and forcible departure, and the other, on the contrary, will experience a brilliant, joyful and favourable departure. How different the two experiences are!

A pit of Hellfire or a garden of Paradise!

The ascetic sheikh of whom we write here, spent his entire lifetime dedicated to serving the mission and guiding man to Al’lah’s Way.

He had never succumbed to the temptations of this lower life nor had he been attracted by its pleasures. When he felt that he was approaching the end of his life and that death was approaching, he wanted to unburden himself of his liabilities and write his testament according to Al’lah’s Saying, “It is prescribed that when death approaches one of you, if they leave property [they should make] a proper bequest to parents and close relatives – a duty incumbent on those who are mindful of God.” ﴿19﴾

And His Saying in another verse, “[In all cases, the distribution comes] after payment of any bequests or debts, with no harm done to anyone: this is a Commandment from God: God is All-Knowing and All- Patient.” ﴿20﴾

He considered the people around him, yet failed to find anyone more dear to him than the venerable master and scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho, for he had made certain of his being one of Al’lah’s great, wise and merciful saints.

The sheikh realised the scholar had been Al’lah’s Gift to the people of this time. This realisation made the sheikh turn, one day, to the noble master who was standing beside where he was seated and say to him, ‘My son, give me your hand please!’

Mohammad Amin thought that he was asking for his help to stand up, so he offered it to him, but instantly the sheikh drew it close to be kissed.

‘Oh, my sheikh... my sheikh! What are you doing? I ask Al’lah for His Forgiveness!’

‘My son! Truly, you are my sheikh and this is my duty towards you,’ said Sheikh Amin Kuftaro.

This incident was witnessed by the friend of the noble Mohammad Amin, Mohammad al-Taghlibi, whose eyes shed tears of joy at the sincerity of what he had just seen.

We mentioned this incident with no intention of digressing, but simply with the aim of elucidating, so now we return to continue our story:

Sheikh Amin Kuftaro had sent for our noble master and another close acquaintance of them both, Mohammad al- Taghlibi, to witness the writing of the sheikh’s testament.

Shortly before that he had summoned one of his disciples to whom the pious sheikh owed nine Ottoman liras.

Scholar Mohammad Amin dressed in a hurry in response to the summons of Sheikh Amin Kuftaro and set off for his house. On the way, he was joined by his dear friend Mohammad al-Taghlibi who was also ready to go out.

Scholar Mohammad Amin said to him, ‘Sheikh Amin has sent for me and I am going to see him now.’

Mohammad al-Taghlibi said, ‘Me too! He has already summoned me, so let’s go together.’

They continued on their way until they reached the house of the elderly sheikh, where they met with the creditor who was already sitting there, having just arrived.

The elderly sheikh addressed them saying, ‘My sons! I feel my time of death is very near and that I’ll soon depart this world, so I want you to witness my testament. My sons: I want this house, which is mine, to be sold and with the money received, I want two small houses to be bought for my two sons: Saleh and Ahmad after repaying my debt to this man. So, I want you Abu Fathi to pay him nine golden Ottoman liras from the price of the house, immediately after its sale and before anything else, as I swear by God, my son, that this debt truly feels like a millstone on my heart; then you can dispose of the rest of the sum as I’ve just told you.’

The creditor immediately exclaimed, ‘Oh sir! May God grant you a long life... money is worth nothing compared to your eminence!’

The noble master, Mohammad Amin, addressed the congenial sheikh saying, ‘Never mind sir! You owe him nothing, as I’ve paid him all his money.’ With that, he put his noble hand into his pocket, drew out a bag and gave it to the man who found that it contained exactly nine liras.

With his pure features overwhelmed with signs of gratitude and affection, and with abundant tears flowing down his cheeks, Sheikh Amin Kuftaro looked at the esteemed Mohammad Amin and began to invoke God’s Blessings for him saying, ‘May Al’lah grant you success my son... may He help you achieve your aims Abu Fathi, and manifest to your heart as He did with those to whom He gave observational knowledge about His Supreme Attributes.’ ﴿21﴾

chapters.title: Who Dares to Challenge the Envoys of God Will Never Succeed
chapters.html:
The story we are going to relate here is about an evil man who felt he had to cease his wrongdoing and evil ways and stop committing crimes against people. This came about because of all that he learned of the outstanding deeds of the solemn officer Mohammad Amin Sheikho when he chastised and defeated the criminals and wrongdoers of the country where he was charged with upholding peace and security. This news crushed the man’s devils and planted terror in his heart since the criminals who were arrested or forced to hide from our brave officer, or even flee the country to avoid coming face to face with him, were more powerful and more deep-rooted in criminality and evil than he was; in fact, many of them were leaders of large, powerful criminal gangs.

Indeed, the actions of the great officer Mohammad Amin were the talk of the people of that time, and the people of Damascus continued to speak of them for many a year to come. The elderly men who had witnessed these events and had them imprinted in their memory still remember them in great detail even to this day. They cannot forget how the dauntless officer punched the leader of the criminals, Humo Jumo, a single blow which caused him to fall to the ground unconscious, and then dragged him by the leg to the prison; at the time the officer was unarmed and the criminal was heavily-armed.

This is just one deed among many that this officer of outstanding character achieved singlehandedly when arresting many evil bands and taking them to prison.

And so, it was that Abu Enad, the criminal in question, decided not to break the law any more as long as Mohammad Amin Sheikho remained the officer in charge of the security of the city of Damascus. Indeed, the habit of the great officer to show no leniency to criminals acted as a bridle for Abu Enad that reined in his spirit whenever it whispered evil things to him out of its foolish pride, thus avoiding confrontation with the venerable master.

Days became months, and months rolled into years and finally it was time for the great officer to retire and receive his pension.

Mohammad Amin was in the habit of attending the lessons of Sheikh Amin Kuftaro (may God have mercy upon him), from the very first time he met him, and he helped in establishing a large circle of followers around the sheikh and granted them every assistance he could offer: power, money and even science.

And so, the place where sheikh Amin used to meet with his disciples was originally only a small basement room, but with the help of Mohammad Amin it grew to become a big mosque in a large, attractive building, and their circle became the biggest in the city.

In front of this mosque, there was a shop belonging to the felon Abu Enad. It was the biggest grocery store at that time and sold a variety of fruits and vegetables. A group of men who were every bit as evil as Abu Enad used to visit him in his store and pass their time there every day, trying to outdo one another in boasting of their evil deeds; and so he became their leader.

The quality of violation is deeply rooted in the spirits of evil people so their devils always urge them to do whatever causes them to become bitter by arousing inside them feelings of hatred, rancour and envy. And so, it was that the spirit of the criminal Abu Enad tempted him against Sheikh Kuftaro and his disciples, especially after he noticed their new, improved situation and the bounties Al’lah had given them at the hands of the dignified master Mohammad Amin.
