He was not pleased to see them enjoying a comfortable and happy life, so he began to use foul language within the hearing of the disciples of the good-hearted sheikh who passed by his store, seeking to pick a quarrel with them and create a bad atmosphere in front of the mosque.

He continued with this bad behaviour until the day came when he dared to act in the same way with the lion, Mohammad Amin, as if he wanted to experience for himself the truth of what he had heard about him.

As usual, the criminal and his friends, who were as bad as he was, were sitting together in front of the grocery store when Mohammad Amin Sheikho appeared in the distance accompanied by his two young sons who were still below the age of fifteen, and also by Abdul-Hadi al-Bani and Basheer al-Khawleh who were youths at that time.

When they passed in front of the store, the criminal Abu Enad knitted his brows and glared at them. His looks were like those usually seen on the faces of belligerent opponents ready for a fierce quarrel. When Mohammad Amin saw him doing this he stopped in his tracks and stared at him with a firm and penetrating look as a divine, awe-inspiring appearance seemed to have been thrown over him so that no-one would dare to display his worst degrees of criminality and tyranny. In fact, this type of confrontation was a face-off between right and wrong, and the miscreant, Abu Enad, soon bowed his head for his evil, arrogant attitude had been routed. Thereupon, the solemn master continued walking, followed by his companions, heading towards the mosque in order to join the prayers. But since base spirits persist in leading their people to destruction, the spirit of this criminal continued to entice him to challenge the human master. He thought, ‘If I could insult Amin Bey before people’s eyes they would be even more afraid of me, and then many men would come under my leadership.’

The idea seemed fair to him so he intended to put it into action.

Ten days had passed after his initial failure to challenge Mohammad Amin when Abu Enad once again saw the venerable master approaching from afar with the same companions as previously. As they were passing his store he seized the opportunity and uttered a profanity that expressed his anger and degradation – indeed, there is a saying that “Every container oozes what it contains.”

On hearing the felon’s foul language, Mohammad Amin stopped in his tracks and turned towards him saying, ‘You, dog! I will not answer you for the moment, for it’s time for prayer and I do not want to miss it; but if you really are a man, stay here until I come out from the mosque, and then... by God... by God ﴿22﴾

I’ll show you what the answer will be!’

Abu Enad, along with all his cronies who were sitting with him, was shocked to hear this intense threat... from the scholar, of all people!... and their faces turned deathly pale. Truly, the foolish, evil grocer had brought misfortune upon himself and he began to experience horrible moments that he would never forget. He did not know how his power and pride had suddenly deserted him on seeing the face of the stately master flaming with anger... he began to shake all over and was afraid that he might pass out. What had happened in reality was that the revered master had given Abu Enad such a sharp, piercing look that it burnt

his evil company, the djinn-kind, who could delude him because of the vice and blindness of his inner self, and destroyed the badness which had been settled in his heart.

As a result, the felon shuddered and lost his power. He felt as if the flames of Hell were burning inside his evil heart and he could not remain steadfast before that powerful gaze.

This was sure to happen, for there is no evil-hearted person that can bear such a look, in fact they would prefer the earth to open and swallow them up than to be faced with a situation similar to that which Abu Enad went through.

And so, a short time before the congregation were due to come out of the mosque, Abu Enad quickly closed his grocery store and turned tail, for fear of facing the brave master. He had learnt a great and lasting lesson, one which wiped out both his pride and his insolence. And here, it must be said that after that time he avoided sitting in front of his store at the times of the lectures of Sheikh Kuftaro in the mosque, as he also refrained from making trouble for all passers-by.

Abu Enad realised that the awe-inspiring appearance with which Almighty Al’lah cloaked this venerable master was the secret that allowed him to grab the reins of security matters in Damascus with a strong fist so that all ill-intentioned people had a thousand reasons to be apprehensive of him.

How could they dare to challenge him when they saw him as a master for religious scholars and a chastiser for criminals, unless they repented and refrained from their wayward conduct; and if they did so he became a guide and teacher for them.

This incident reminds us of a similar one that our great Prophet Mohammad (cpth) faced and resolved by the aweinspiring appearance God placed on him. Those who related the story told of a man of the Irash clan, ﴿23﴾

who came to Mecca driving some camels with him. When Abu Jahl ben Hisham, ﴿24﴾

a notable man of the people of Quraysh, saw this man, he took a camel on the pretence of buying one but failed to pay for it.

The man went to a gathering place for the people of Quraysh, the famous tribe in Mecca, and addressed the men there, saying, ‘People of Quraysh! Is there a man among you that may help me get what is rightly due to me from Abu al-Hakam ﴿25﴾

ben Hisham? I am a traveller here. I know nobody here to ask for help, and that man took advantage of me and refused to give me what is rightfully mine.’

The men in the assembly hall answered in a careless manner, attempting to mock the stranger. ‘Do you see that man?’ and they pointed to the Envoy of God, Mohammad (cpth), who was sitting to one side of the Holy Mosque, and they then continued, ‘Go to him. He is the one who can force Abu al-Hakam to restore your rights.’ They were well aware of the hostile feelings that Abu Jahl had in his heart for the Envoy of God (cpth) and their intention was to make the stranger an object of ridicule.

As for the Envoy of God, when the man in need walked towards him and laid his case before him he quickly got to his feet and walked towards the house of Abu Jahl while the wronged man hurriedly followed him.

When the people of Quraysh saw what was happening they told one of the men among them to follow Mohammad to see what he would do. When the Prophet (cpth) reached the house of Abu Jahl he knocked at the door and then turned his back and stood there waiting for the answer. The voice of Abu Jahl came from inside asking, ‘Who’s that?’

‘It’s me, Mohammad,’ the Prophet replied, ‘Come out.’

Abu Jahl soon opened the door, but something strange was happening!

Before the Envoy of God could utter a single word about his reason for knocking at the door, the face of Abu Jahl turned deathly pale and his entire body trembled with fear!

The Prophet (cpth) addressed him saying, ‘Come on! Give this man what is due to him.’

Abu Jahl replied with a shaking voice, ‘Yes... yes... I will... stay here to see that I will give him his money in full.’

He left them outside and went back into his house. And within just a few minutes he came out to the Envoy (cpth) holding the correct amount in his hand and gave it to the man. Thereupon, the Envoy (cpth) turned towards the man saying, ‘Is it your due sum in full?’

‘Yes it is,’ the wronged man answered, ‘Yes, sir, it is the full amount! Thank you sir, thank you very much.’

The Envoy (cpth) walked on his way leaving the traveller who headed towards the assembly place of the people of Quraysh and said to them, ‘May God give Mohammad the best reward for what he did to me. He helped me to get the full amount owed to me.’

The assembled men looked at each other in utter disbelief! But then, when the man they had sent to watch what would happen between the Prophet (cpth) and their comrade Abu Jahl, came back and told them about Abu Jahl’s strange reaction towards the Envoy (cpth) and how he was trembling with terror, their wonder grew more and more.

After a short time, Abu Jahl came to the same gathering place and when the men there saw him they rushed towards him asking, ‘Hey, man! What’s the matter with you? By God, we’ve never seen a man that reacted as you did! What happened to you?’

Abu Jahl said, ‘Listen well! You didn’t see what I saw. By God, when Mohammad came to my house and knocked on the door, I felt my heart drop down to my boots the moment that I heard his voice calling me, and when I opened the door I saw what appeared to be a lion hovering over his head... it was massive, with bared fangs the like of which I swear that I have never seen before. By God, I felt that if I had refused to give the wayfarer what was due to him, the lion would have definitely devoured me.’

In short, and in fact, the Almighty Al’lah had thrown a divine, awe-inspiring raiment over His Successor. So, is there anyone that dares to stand in the way of the Envoy of God (cpth), whether they be individuals or entire nations.

chapters.title: The Disciple Repeats the Sheikh’s Lesson
chapters.html:
God, the Almighty, created humanity in the most perfect composition. He gave mankind the aptitude to acquire virtue and perfection, and endowed them with the ability to receive and retain great shares of His Supreme Attributes.

This perfect composition also includes the capacity with which God supported the human spirit and which allows it to reach a high degree of knowledge about the Supreme Being. God designated this composition for humankind alone, for there is no other kind of creation that has received this gift. Not even the noble angels can compete with humanity in their ability to be the nearest to their Provider, or have spirits more able to bear the Godly Manifestation, or witness wider realms of perfection indicated by His Supreme Names, than the human spirit.

God says in a Holy Saying, “Not My heavens nor My earth could bear My Manifestion; only the heart of My believing obedient follower could.”

The Almighty has supplied mankind with the power of thought and provided them with various precious faculties; He also granted them insight and put before them universal signs to help them recognise Him after He made their spirits more firm and more powerful than all other spirits of creation. What is more, He honoured them with the freedom of choice and, unlike animal-kind, did not entrust the management of their affairs to other creatures. God overwhelmed humanity with these bounties in order to help them witness the worlds of Godly Perfection and enjoy witnessing His Beautiful Attributes, a vision that makes mankind soar, enraptured by this High Treasure, for evermore.

In another Holy Saying, He - Glory to Him - says, “I was a hidden Treasure; I liked to be known so I created the creation and acquainted them with Me. Thus through Me they could recognise Me.”

Oh Mankind, you were created for this purpose. God bestowed on you intellect, understanding, a nature disposed to loving perfection, and best constitution so that you can ascend ever higher and tower up in spirit over the rest of creation. In the world of al-Azal, the world of first creation, God offered the freedom of choice to all spirits. Only human-kind, willingly and voluntarily, accepted it and supported it. Therefore, God destined them for a high level of dignity and distinguished them from the rest of creation.

The noble companions of God’s Envoy (cpth) had risen in rank until they were able to attain this dignity. They took perfect advantage of the gifts with which God endowed them equally, as He did with all other humans; and this enabled them to release their spirits from the control of the physical body and material existence. The gentle light of their spirits could overcome the thick veil of the body and all worldly matters that might otherwise prevent them from seeing realities. Thus their heart’s-eye was opened and their spirits become pure and elevated. Loving and yearning, they rushed to do every possible good deed, having previously formed a loathing of all that was detestable, and disliked those who practised such things. Therefore they lived a highly sanctified life filled with heart pleasure and spiritual comfort for which all the kings of the world would, gladly and willingly, have abdicated their thrones had they been aware of it. Yes, indeed! The spirits of these noble companions became so sensitive and receptive that no communication equipment anywhere in the world, however great it is, might be compared with them. The following is a story confirming this truth in all its importance:

Before starting his weekly Friday lesson, Sheikh Amin Kuftaro noticed the absence of his faithful follower, Mohammad Amin Sheikho. It was the first time he did not see his illustrious disciple at his lectures; so he asked his followers if they knew where the young master could be.

‘He is ill, sir,’ some of them replied. ‘He is confined to bed, so he cannot come.’

Sheikh Amin said, ‘Oh, may God heal him. Truly, he is a pious and pure man, marked with holy perfection.’

Then he began to relate the new weekly lesson which he had prepared for his murids after uttering the statement, ‘I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan.’

Our pure man, Mohammad Amin, was accustomed to attending the lectures of his sheikh, Amin Kuftaro, a goodhearted God-fearing guide, where he listened to his explanations about God’s Words, the Holy Qur’an. But because of the illness he was suffering from this week, he could not go to the mosque and was obliged to stay in his bed. The young Mohammad Amin was so loving and faithful to his sheikh and he was always the first to arrive at every lecture and the last to leave. Because of their love for him and wanting to be reassured about his health, when Sheikh Amin Kuftaro finished his lesson of guidance, his followers discussed the matter of their brother Mohammad Amin and decided that some of them should be appointed to go, on behalf of all the group to visit him at home and enquire about his health.

The selected group duly headed off toward Mohammad Amin’s house and went to his room. The young man was still in bed suffering from intense pains. They greeted him and wished him a speedy recovery and then they sat around him and began to look at him without uttering a single word. A feeling of awe and reverence crept into their hearts while they were looking at the young man; he, too, remained silent, looking at them with eyes full of kindness, compassion and tenderness. Despite his undoubted suffering, his face was glowing with happiness and light which brought pleasure to the hearts of those who were gazing at him.

Time passed, moment by moment while a strange, but cosy, air of calmness and silence still prevailed in the room.

Having noticed that no one spoke, our gracious man barely managed to pull his body up to a sitting position; whereupon one of the visitors rushed towards him and put a pillow behind his back to help him to sit more comfortably. Eventually the silence was broken when a calm, soothing voice, overflowing with happiness and true heart-life, issued from the virtuous mouth of our humane man, saying ,

‘I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan.’

How strange! His voice and accent were exactly the same as those of Sheikh Amin Kuftaro, their pure guide! This immediately caught the full attention of the attendance who turned towards our man in amazement.

With calm and poignant words, the young man continued to speak, breathing spiritual life and joy into the hearts of those around him. Sometimes he spoke very gently, expressing great affection and tenderness, and at other times he remained silent for a while. With every word he uttered the listeners grew more attentive and fascinated; it seemed that they were mesmerised and immersed in a holy sea! No doubt, in that room there was something very strange and unusual that attracted their attention and caused their amazement, thus making them concentrate all their senses on our noble human being and his pure, sweet words.

For a full hour the young man continued to talk while all those present remained silent, looking at him with inquiring eyes until he finished speaking. There and then, the audience began to whisper to each other disclosing the secret that had brought them to that strange state of wonderment. Truly it was something that bewildered their minds! The speech of the young man Mohammad Amin was a full and exact repetition of the lesson they had already heard two hours ago from their guide, Sheik Amin Kuftaro.

Mohammad Amin had been absent from this lesson because of his illness and the other disciples came to his home directly after their sheikh had finished his teaching; so how could he, when he was confined to bed, too weak to leave it, recite exactly the same lesson his sheikh had recited without adding or subtracting a single word... not a word more and not a word less? What aroused even more amazement was that he was reciting the lesson in the same tone of voice as that of their sheikh which was imprinted on their minds! He even made the same gestures and demonstrated the same emotions that Sheikh Amin had showed when he was particularly affected by the words he recited. He paused his speech at precisely the same points their sheikh had stopped at, and each pause took the same period of time for both of them! So, the lesson repeated by Mohammad Amin took exactly one full hour as it did the first time they heard it from the mouth of their sheikh!

This was the cause of the overwhelming astonishment created inside their spirits that made everyone of them talk about it and begin to whisper to his neighbour in the seat beside him. They all inquired about the secret behind this miracle and, indeed, behind this pure and pious human being. No doubt, he had achieved such a high degree of godliness and illumination by God’s Light that it enabled him to recite the same new lesson as his sheikh although he was in bed when the lesson was given and could not have heard even one word of it.

Had there been recording equipment at that time (the early years of the twentieth century), it could not have played a more accurate reproduction of the sheikh’s lesson than what was recited by this venerable master, a man known for his high prestige and impeccable truthfulness.

Indeed, the achievements of true belief are far higher than all those of human science and invention.

And truly, humanity will never achieve perfection except by belief; and by belief alone will they enjoy worldly and After-worldly blessings, for all eternity.

chapters.title: This Man Gave Us His Full Support
chapters.html:
When the venerable master Mohammad Amin met with Sheikh Amin Kuftaro (may God have mercy upon him) he sensed his good-heartedness and virtuous merits, and his faithfulness in calling people to God. Therefore Mohammad Amin put himself at his service with all the wealth, power and knowledge of science that he possessed. And from that time on he supported him wholeheartedly.

He spared no effort when it came to acquainting people with the good sheikh and spent generously to invite them to attend his circle until, after hard work and sufferance on his side, it became the largest of all the religious circles of that time.

The venerable master, Mohammad Amin, realised that this honest sheikh was the best man and the most appropriate guide for the people of that age, for he would be able to help them follow the right path. The people of Syria believed in the principle, “He who follows the steps of a religious scholar will be in a state of grace when he meets God.” What this means is that a man will keep himself on the straight path. His deeds and acts will be far removed from causing any evil to befall anyone and, as a result, there would be no sins and no breaches of God’s Statutes.

The mosque of Sheikh Amin Kuftaro, which was called Abu al-Nur Mosque, was only a small, windowless, cellar which needed to be lit with candles even in the middle of the day. But when a great crowd of people gathered around the good-hearted sheikh and began to attend his lessons, the noble master, Mohammad Amin, decided to work towards the expansion of the mosque so that it would be spacious enough to hold the ever increasing number of disciples. He gave every assistance possible to this purpose, either financially or through his personal influence.

He brought workers and builders to build and plaster the walls; he cut the poplar trees of the orchard he had inherited from his father in al-Hamah county and brought the wood to be used in the building. He worked towards constructing a large summer balcony that could hold a great number of the congregation. This was in addition to many other deeds he accomplished, until eventually the mosque was made much bigger and fully refurbished, all of which was carried out at his own expense.

The good-hearted sheikh, Amin Kuftaro, regarded the humane master Mohammad Amin as a mercy that God the Almighty sent to him, not only because of the money and the power which Mohammad Amin sacrificed in order to improve the circle, but also because he became a source of Godly Science, to the extent that the sheikh began to rely on this in his teaching.

This actually happened after the venerable master frequently corrected his sheikh in relation to his explanation of the Qur’anic verses, but he was sure to do so discreetly and with the utmost degree of politeness and kindness. An example of one of these times of correction was when the good-hearted sheikh tried to explain the noble verse, “Alas for the servants! Whenever an Envoy comes to them they ridicule him.” ﴿26﴾

He said within the hearing of the congregation, ‘See my sons how great the Mercy of God is! See how He laments for His servants who strayed from the right path.’

When the venerable master Mohammad Amin heard this explanation he did not accept its significance nor its reasoning. He clearly understood the meaning of contrition, and so it could never be ascribed to God for it did not correspond with His Perfection and Supreme Attributes. He knew well that when one feels contrition towards somebody it means that they were negligent in their duties towards those for whom they care. For example, the student who neglected his studies and consequently failed in the final exam will censure himself. This is because he should have studied in order to avoid failure, yet he was too lazy and negligent to do so.

As for Al’lah (Glory to Him), He is absolutely far above being neglectful of His creatures, and so He does not feel contrition because of their destination.

The true interpretation in the view of the clear-sighted master is that the unbelievers themselves will repent and live in a state of grief and remorse because they had the chance to believe and follow the Envoys of God but instead they chose to follow the easy path and denied the true guidance. As a result, they remained far from God and deprived themselves of the Garden He has prepared for them.

In his gentle, polite way, the venerable master Mohammad Amin went to Sheikh Amin Kuftaro after the lecture had finished and said to him, ‘Oh Sheikh, I’m so concerned that I may become irreligious.’

Sheikh Amin said, ‘You, son? No... never! I could believe that of anyone else in the world, but not of you, oh... no, not at all.’

Master Mohammad Amin said, ‘Oh Sheikh, but I feel that my spirit did not accept the explanation that you gave about the verse you mentioned during the lesson.’

Then he began to elucidate to the sheikh the points he felt to be erroneous in the explanation and then clarified what he thought to be the right meaning.

Sheikh Amin pondered on the words of the venerable master and found them all to be true; so he said to him, ‘By God, my son, you are right and it is me who is in the wrong.

You have given the truest explanation of the verse whereas I have not. If God wills, I will correct the explanation I gave in the next lecture.’

The repetition of similar situations of correction to the meanings of many Qur’anic verses made Sheikh Amin say to Mohammad Amin, ‘My son, I want you to sit in the first row of seats and keep looking at me as long as I make correct statements, but if you hear me saying something that is wrong, just turn your eyes away from me.’

And so, that was really what went on secretly between the sheikh and the venerable master. Whenever Sheikh Amin gave an erroneous meaning of a noble verse relying on books of narrated sayings and stories, Mohammad Amin would simply avert his eyes and then the sheikh would stop talking and resort to God to inspire him to give the right meaning. If he was guided to the right explanation, he would continue with his speech and correct the meaning.

But sometimes Sheikh Amin failed to find the right meaning so he would say to his disciples, ‘Listen, my sons, I will speak about this issue again in the next lecture, if God wills it.’

Then he would sit with the revered master, Mohammad Amin, who would always be happy to clarify the true meaning for him.

In this way, Mohammad Amin became like a guide and teacher for the good-hearted sheikh who depended on him and sought help from him. Such is the habit of believers; they are all as one body, supporting one another.

This situation made the relationship between the two good men grow firmer and stronger, but it did not please the envious disciples in Sheikh Amin’s circle who spared no effort to be close to the heart of their sheikh, but all their efforts came to nothing.

They kissed the hand of their sheikh and carried his bag whenever he entered the hall, they never missed his lectures and insisted on writing them down in full, however they could not hope to get closer to the heart of their sheikh than Master Mohammad Amin.

Eventually, their jealousy went so deep that finding no other way to win the heart of their guide, they began to plot against the honest master in order to stir up antagonism between him and their guide. Thus, in the presence of the sheikh and before all those present at his lectures, they decided to accuse Mohammad Amin of stealing. Actually, during one of the lectures, one of those spiteful men began to speak badly about the august master, Mohammad Amin, and accused him of being sly, in the hearing of Sheikh Amin Kuftaro.

When Mohammad Amin heard the false charge that the envious men tried to accuse him with, a feeling like a horrible whirlwind shook him violently and he was about to answer them, but out of respect for his sheikh he controlled himself and turned to them saying in a threatening voice, ‘I will not answer you now, but when you come out of this meeting, I will show you.’

The threat issued by Mohammad Amin annoyed the good-hearted sheikh, so he looked at Mohammad Amin and said, ‘Get out, I don’t want to see you in my chamber.’

Absolute silence followed the words of Sheikh Amin and every disciple present in the room turned to look at Mohammad Amin, waiting for his reaction. Mohammad Amin remained as though rooted to the spot, in absolute silence. When Sheikh Amin saw that the noble master did not leave he repeated his words, ‘I’ve told you to leave my chamber... I do not want you here.’

Yet despite the repetition, the noble master kept sitting there resolutely, silent and motionless. Even after he heard the same request repeated for the third time Mohammad Amin still did not react.

The good-hearted sheikh began to look at the noble master without saying another word. When he saw that he had no intention of budging from the spot, he leaped up, his fury and nervousness displayed clearly on his face and in his actions. He then charged ahead and stormed out of the chamber.

He entered his own room and closed the door behind him. This scene took place while all the attendance were still in their places watching the two men in astonishment.

They stared at Mohammad Amin with looks that displayed their shock and awe in equal measure, waiting to see what might happen in such a critical situation.

The kindly sheikh remained out of sight for a quarter of an hour and then he came out of his room and returned to the hall with a face quite free of any trace of nervousness or excitement. The anger which had overwhelmed him had entirely vanished. He rejoined his disciples in a calm manner and took his seat. He then looked up and addressed his disciples saying, ‘My sons, listen to me carefully,’ and pointing at Mohammad Amin he continued by saying, ‘By God... by God, this man has granted us every assistance. He depleted his own wealth and prestige in order to elevate this circle, and now he helps us with science. So, whoever seeks to recognise God should refer to this man. I sincerely mean what I say, and I repeat that whoever wants to know about Al’lah should refer to this man.’

The good-hearted sheikh retracted his negative attitude towards Mohammad Amin, for the true believer always checks his words and actions, and pulls back from those that are wrong.

However, this was not the only time that the venerable master had been placed in such a difficult position, for he experienced many similar situations during his attendance in the circle. However, he bore patiently the mistakes of Sheikh Amin towards him until the day finally came when he found himself unable to bear any more. He carefully considered what he should do and decided that it would be preferable for him to leave the circle of Sheikh Amin and he went to bed having decided on this course of action.

While he was asleep he saw the Prophet Mohammad (cpth): he (cpth) appeared with his noble palm covering his pure mouth, hiding a gentle smile, while a frown appeared in the compassionate eyes of his august face, he (cpth) said to Mohammad Amin while pointing to Sheikh Amin Kuftaro with the other hand, ‘This is the way to me. Whoever comes to me without passing through him will not enter.’

Mohammad Amin awoke immediately after this moving dream and he soon reversed his decision. Although he was to come up against further difficult situations with the sheikh, Mohammad Amin bore them all with great patience. If, sometimes, his spirit whispered to him to leave the company of Sheikh Amin because of his mistakes, he used to ask it, ‘Is he an infallible Prophet?’ And the answer would come from deep within him, ‘No.’

‘So...’, he continued to speak to himself saying, ‘then I have to stay with him.’ He remained with Sheikh Amin and never separated from him until the latter departed this earthly life and moved to the Presence of his Noble Lord.

During that era, the great majority of people were simple and good-hearted. They were inclined to the religion by imitating religious scholars rather than by way of deep self analysis. It was enough for them to confess that there is no god except Al’lah, to pray, to fast, to give alms, and to go to Mecca for pilgrimage if they were able to travel. There were no forbidden acts in public streets during that time, and to add to the sense of well-being the prevailing atmosphere among the people was one of purity and virtue.

These circumstances were sufficient for a gentle, goodhearted guide like Sheikh Amin Kuftaro to turn people towards God and to make a positive impression on their hearts. Actually, Sheikh Amin was most successful in urging people to persist in obeying God and avoiding all His Prohibitions. For this reason, Mohammad Amin acted only as a supporter and aide for the goodly sheikh and helped him secretly to elevate the whole circle.

The time for disclosing his divine sciences and the lofty and supreme guidance he acquired from God had not yet arrived as the devilish schools had not yet come into existence. But later, when the foreign-organised schools of seduction or infidelity began to be established in an attempt to defame the religion of Islam by means of science, it was time for the great scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho, whom Al’lah had destined for such a time, to speak in public. The time eventually came for the flood of divine sciences to stand up to those negative calls and refute them after they began to have an adverse effect on the people’s minds through the various means of technology, and alienate them from the right Statute of God.

In fact, Mohammad Amin brought true sciences that uplift those of sound judgement to high levels. He revealed that the performance of good deeds is the only way which leads to Paradise according to God’s Saying in His noble verses, “Enter Paradise for what you have been doing.” ﴿27﴾

And, “This is the Garden you have been given as your own because of what you used to do.” ﴿28﴾

And, that the rules and laws of Islam are not simply blind acts of worship, the wisdom of which is incomprehensible to mankind.

Rather, the basis of this religion, every movement, every word and every rite has its own lofty indication and desired outcome, and each has a wisdom that makes it indispensible and a proof that distinguishes it.

The basic tenet of the religion of Islam is the statement that there is no god except Al’lah and that Mohammad is God’s Envoy for it includes deep meanings and an indispensible reality for the believer, and that prayer has a fruitful outcome, otherwise it would be a senseless religious duty. Almsgiving has its purpose and benefits, too, and so do fasting and pilgrimage, both of which pave the way for every believer to become illuminated by the Light of Al’lah.

And so, all that is mentioned in God’s Legislation has wisdom and a purpose which the Almighty has assigned to it, and generated the dire need for it within humanity. All this is apart from the exalted meanings of the verses of the Holy Qur’an which show the highest degree of perfection, and reveal the impeccability of the great Prophets.

In reality, the humane scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho led us to stand before an ocean of Godly Science, which is filled with abundant goodness and limitless knowledge. When faced with such manifest realities one can understand that they have only to follow the rules of the religion in order to ascend to the highest ranks of transcendence, such as the noble companions of the Prophets followed and actually attained.

It is noticeable that the time in which we are living now is entirely different from the time when life was distinguished by its simplicity, and even naivety. In such a climate, when the way of living and mankind’s thought processes were far less complex, the miraculous acts which God sometimes reveals only at the hands of the people of religion, work advantageously in people’s hearts. Therefore the Almighty showed the people of that time what they liked to see and would never deny, unusual events brought to them through the hands of good men since the wiles of Satan had not yet begun to circulate.

Sheikh Amin Kuftaro experienced his share of these miracles, and here are some of them:

One day, as he was walking along the street, he passed by a house when suddenly a little boy opened the street door from inside. Unintentionally, Sheikh Amin caught a glimpse of a female through the opened door but he cast down his glance immediately. Nevertheless, he felt sad and gloomy, and began to blame himself for what had happened. He regarded himself as a sinner because he had looked at the female although it was out of his control; therefore he asked his Lord to make him blind as a kind of penance to forgive him for the misdeed he had committed.

The Almighty responded to him and caused him to lose his sight. He remained blind for six months during which he experienced the difficult state which the blind live in. After these hard months he withdrew his request and invoked his Lord to restore his sight once again. Actually, as soon as he finished his petition, the Almighty answered him and restored his sight.

In another incident, when people were in the habit of storing what they would need of staple foodstuff, such as wheat for flour, lentils and bulgur, and storing them in large, deep vessels, Sheikh Amin Kuftaro bought sufficient staple foods for his family to last for an entire year, taking into consideration any guests who might come to his home as he was a hospitable man who frequently received and entertained visitors. It was well known that whoever visited him would not be allowed to leave without partaking of food and drink.

At the end of the year, Sheikh Amin asked his family to check the storage vessels to see if there was any food remaining or if they were empty. When they checked them they found they were all full to the brim with grain without any space for more.

Another miracle took place with this good-hearted sheikh when, once, a group of Christian people got into a disagreement with a group of Muslims about a Christian man that had died and was to be buried. The Christians wanted to bury the man in question in their graveyard whereas the Muslims refused and insisted on burying him in theirs.

In the view of the Muslim group, the deceased had confessed Islam before his death, and so he had departed this life as a Muslim and not as a Christian. As for the Christians, they objected to the Muslims’ claim and still considered the dead man to be their son and one of their kinfolk; and so they, and not any other sect, had the full right to bury him in their own cemetery.

The dead man was in the coffin while the two parties were engaged in a fruitless discussion about his final resting place. Each party presented its proofs, and yet they could not reach an agreement or find a solution that might please them both.

This continued until one of the group cried out, ‘Oh people... oh men!’ The protagonists all stopped talking and turned towards the source of this shout. Thereupon, the man suggested, ‘Do you all agree to let the first man to pass this way give us a judgement about this problem and then for everyone to accept it whatever it will be?’ The two sides answered in unison, ‘Yes, we do,’ for they really wanted to put an end to the controversy. They remained where they were, the dead man in his coffin, gazing at the road in wait for the first person to come that way.

It was God’s Will that He sent Sheikh Amin Kuftaro along the way we have mentioned. When the crowd saw him they rushed towards him and laid the case before him, then they asked him to judge the problem and offer them a solution.

The sheikh (may God have mercy upon him) looked into the matter and pondered upon it, then he replied, ‘I see that the party carrying the coffin will have the right to bury the deceased in their graveyard.’ The two parties agreed on this judgement, and first the relatives of the departed soon advanced towards the coffin and bent down to lift it, but how strange!

They could not raise it at all! Many members of their group came forward to help and together they all tried repeatedly to lift the coffin... but their efforts came to nothing! Thereupon, they gave up and stood aside leaving the other party to take their turn to lift the coffin. The crowd of Muslims walked towards the casket and then a few of them bent down to lift it up.

It was a great shock for the Christians when they saw that just a few Muslims were able to lift the coffin with great ease.

Thus, the Muslims marched happily towards their graveyard with the coffin carried on their shoulders until they reached the place of burial and buried the departed; in the meantime, the eyes of the Christian relatives and friends of the dead person were following them, watching in overwhelming and absolute silence.

chapters.title: An Honourable Outcome.
chapters.html:
“Be Merciful Toward a Noble Man that Has Become Humble”

It is said that ‘There is no god but Al’lah’ and this is manifested by His Providing Presence that creates all creatures through His great Bounty, to be firmly connected and full of virtues and goodness.

Man was the first one destined to receive this bonus when he was taken from Paradise to the world of shapes and material bodies so that he might attain deeds of his own free will which will always lead him closer to God through everlasting, sacred communication with Him, and grant him ascent in successive eternal paradises. In this worldly life, man enjoys the blessings bestowed liberally upon him, including the ability to think for himself. The Almighty sent the Prophets and, after them, the noble companions and righteous men to guide him, and He conferred upon him various kinds of benefits as practical lessons for him. Man should know that he is just a visitor to this life: he possesses nothing in it because everything belongs to Al’lah alone, and no-one will remain in this life forever. Any man that turns away from Al’lah and whose heart becomes so blind that his love for this earthly life deafens him to the Call of Al’lah is neglecting his Paradise and loses his accrued benefits when he omits to do good deeds, and fails to think of Al’lah’s Signs and Favours.

Then, in order to guide him, Al’lah withholds some of His Gifts and treats him by afflicting him with misfortune, so that he may come to his senses, repent and invoke God; then his spirit recovers from its diseases by resorting to God, and by loving Him, the Almighty, he becomes a righteous man worthy of Al’lah’s Benefaction. He will receive grace and never forget his Benefactor, thus he becomes a good man who is qualified to do good deeds and follow the path of loving God and His saints, which leads him to the Paradise promised to him.

Times have changed, and life has taken an unexpected turn for a man who once held a position of great authority. The commander, the absolute master, the leader of tough soldiers, the recipient of the large salary, has become humbled, destitute, shabby, and of such low esteem, that people quarrel with him, or even deny his very existence. Officer Mohammad Amin was a man renowned for his righteousness and illustrious reputation. He became the leader and guide of the people and wherever he walked in the districts of Damascus they bowed their heads before him.

One day, he was trying to resolve an incident that had occurred in his quarter, al-Salhiyeh, when he saw the man mentioned above as he was being pushed around by people scornful of his poverty and ragged clothes. Suddenly Officer Mohammad Amin recognised him, ‘Oh God, he’s the commander-in-chief! I don’t believe it! Is this a fitting state for a previous commander to end up in?’

He went towards him calling out, ‘Hello, sir.’ Then he greeted him, kissed him and embraced him.

People hurried to bring a chair for the great master, Mohammad Amin, who settled the dispute immediately, and everyone then went about his own business. The two men remained together and this needy man, who had become so despised, instantly became respectable in the eyes of the people simply because of the company of the venerable master.

They strolled together along the street, and after an amicable chat about their old friendship during military service, the air cleared and the commander’s troubled spirit lightened. Thereupon, Officer Mohammad Amin addressed him, ‘Oh, sir! We were brothers-in-arms and when I was in financial straits I used to come to you for help. I borrowed money from you which I repaid when it was possible.’ He continued to talk to him in this soothing manner and then gave him some golden liras, saying, ‘Make a note of this amount in your accounts book.’ With a mounting feeling of gratitude and self-respect, the commander stretched out his hand and took the golden coins, saying, ‘I’ll accept them only on that condition.’

Mohammad Amin accompanied the man as far as his house, then took his leave and went on his way.

Our righteous man inquired further about the course the commander’s life had taken, and his current situation and financial state. He was told that the owner of the house in which he had been living had tried to throw him out six months earlier as he was not able to pay the rent because his financial state had gone from bad to worse. He had spent all his savings, and even sold the furnishings from his house to provide for his needs as he had no profession whereby he could earn a salary.

In fact, he had sold everything he had in order to feed his family.

Every day, he also bought a bottle of wine along with the food. He used to drink wine until he lost consciousness so as to forget his painful situation and the abject poverty he now faced. He was overcome by despair.

But Officer Mohammad Amin, that wise man who knew God and could put everything into its proper place, remembered the noble Hadith, “Be merciful toward a noble man that has become humble.”

This is why he decided that this man should have a monthly income.

He paid the rent arrears of the house, bought a can of ghee, ﴿29﴾

sent it to the commander’s house, and told him to add the cost to the running account. Besides this, he began to visit him once a month and offered him a fixed amount, but he always found him in a drunken stupor – unable to hear or understand anything; so he did not enter the house.

Six months passed in this manner until the day when he knocked at the door to offer the monthly amount – as usual – whereupon the commander’s young child invited him to enter the house at her father’s request. So, he went in and mounted the stairs to the room of the ex-commander. He found him well-dressed, wearing glasses and reading the Holy Qur’an; when the latter saw him, he closed the Qur’an and hastened to greet him.

The house was now clean and attractive, and the man had started to read the Holy Qur’an. Life had returned to this man whose heart was dead after his spirit had collapsed.

The man who had once been an Ottoman commander took Mohammad Amin by the hand and led him into the room. They sat together and were chatting amicably, when the commander interjected, ‘Oh Bey! I want to tell you my story... it is something incredible. Wine was running through my veins, and the doctors had said that it would be impossible for me to give it up. But three days ago, I raised the cup to drink, and when I drank the wine it tasted like castor oil: it was disgusting. I tried to sip it once again, but I vomited in disgust so I threw the bottle from the window... come and let me show you.’

He took our compassionate officer by the hand and led him to the window where he pointed at the garbage and said, ‘I threw all the wine bottles from the window onto the rubbish pile... finally I have given up drinking wine. Al’lah has cured me and I’ve been created anew. Now I pray and perform all my religious duties, praising God Who has cured me. Yes... I am truly repentant, by God’s Will... Al’lah has cured me... praise is to Him.’

Thus, this former commander-in-chief overcame a serious obstacle and continued his life as a man who observed his religious rites as Al’lah wanted him to do, and according to his spirit’s desire for guidance and righteousness. His reputation was restored to the extent that people called him a “saint”: a virtuous, upright believer, and he remained as such until the day he died.

So, we see that by such sublime treatment and perfect benevolence the great guide, Mohammad Amin, was able to raise this man from a state of wretchedness to one of perfect happiness. Because of his great mercy he helped the excommander when he was humbled after being an eminent, highly respected man. He led him to taste the good life once again and restored to him a sense of honour, therefore the former commander was deeply attached to him and he also turned back to his Provider after a long period of shunning Him; his spirit came to loathe committing sins, and he became one of those who read the Holy Qur’an and pray regularly. He became quite saintly, and as the noble Hadith says, “If Al’lah has guided a man through you, it is something better for you than having all that over which the sun rises.”

Such was the custom of this great master-guide in reforming hearts and leading them to his beloved – Mohammad (cpth), the Envoy – who lets spirits enter into God’s Presence and attain paradises.

chapters.title: The Story of the Deceased who Prayed at His own Funeral
chapters.html:
God says: “When the spirit of the dying man reaches his throat and you, all the while, are looking on – We are nearer to him than you, yet you do not see Us – if you do not find yourselves guilty, you will bring back his spirit if you are truly obedient [to Me].” ﴿30﴾

A close friend of Mohammad Amin had died. He had spent the last two years of his life suffering from terrible, painful ailments.

Mohammad Amin escorted him, sadly, to his grave, and after everyone had left the graveyard, he sat at his friend’s tomb for a long time weeping, then he left with the pain of loss crushing his spirit due to the terrible sadness engulfing his merciful heart.

Once at his home, the extreme grief continued to devastate him, causing him to sit, think of the state of his friend in the grave and weep for him anew. And, finally, exhausted by his continuous weeping at the loss of his friend, he fell into a fitful sleep during which he saw his friend saying to him, ‘Oh my brother! I’m so happy... I’m delighted... it is only your weeping for me that disturbs me... I’m all right.’

Mohammad Amin woke up with a start, disturbed at what he had heard, and began to pray to God, ‘I seek refuge with God from the cursed devil... this dream may be a devil that wants to turn me away from remembering my friend and his painful fate.’ Then he began to weep again until, eventually, his body collapsed from sheer exhaustion. He fell asleep and again he dreamt of his friend who was saying to him, ‘By God I’m very happy but your weeping troubles me... I’m all right... listen: I shall tell you my story so that you do not think I’m a devil that has come to you in a vision.

‘You know that I was ill and paralysed for many years. And eventually I was confined to my bed. When I was lying there, the pain, which had become progressively worse since the beginning of my illness, became unbearable as time went by. I resorted to Al’lah whole-heartedly and then I felt quite sound and healthy... yes, I was fine... I checked my entire body... my arms... my legs... I felt no pain... I regained my health completely... out of my happiness I jumped from my bed onto the floor, and called out to my wife and sons to come and look at me for I had made a full recovery...!

‘But when they came, they paid no attention to me... and the strangest thing was that they went into my room still paying not the least bit of attention to what I was saying... in fact they left me alone outside my room, so, unable to understand their strange behaviour I followed them into the bedroom.

‘They ignored me and threw themselves on the body of a strange man lying on my bed. My wife was unveiled and, accompanied by the children, she was crying piteously. I was furious and shouted, at them trying to make them stop, “Leave him alone... why have you unveiled your face in front of this strange man?” But still they took no notice of me and continued to weep over the stranger.

‘After some time, men came and washed the corpse and I asked them, “Who is this deceased person?” But they didn’t answer me... and they carried the body and put it in the coffin... at that moment I became determined to know the name of the deceased.

‘On the way to the mosque where the funeral prayers would be said for him, something odd occurred! I saw my old friends whom I had not seen for many years. I asked them about the dead man but no one replied... it was as though no-one had heard me, and whenever I spoke to one of them, he broke into tears.’

What was actually happening here was that Mohammad Amin was witnessing the state of his deceased friend and the events and traumas he had undergone. It was his sadness for his friend overflowing from his merciful heart that had led him to this vision from the moment of his death to the present moment.

Our man’s friend continued to recount his story to him, he said, ‘I was determined to know the name of the dead man whom everyone was so concerned about... I asked them about him, but no-one replied.

‘Within a short time, the funeral cortege was ready to pray. They prayed for the deceased and I prayed with them. They then went out of the mosque, and when they reached the graveyard they put the coffin on the ground and took out the corpse to bury it. I resolved to know who he was, even at the last moment... I decided to look at his face when they put him in his grave and I was sure that I would recognise him.

‘The mourners gathered around the grave and I passed through the group and stood on the brink of the grave to see who the dead man was. When the gravedigger uncovered the face of the dead man, I felt great pressure in my head and became giddy which caused me to lose my balance and tumble into the grave, then I cried out, “Help me! Help!” But how strange! They paid no attention to me and began placing the concrete slabs over the grave and covering them with earth.

‘I shouted, “Everyone... listen to me! I’m alive... by God I’m alive... why are you doing this to me?”

‘But they did not respond and they left me in that miserable situation.’

The deceased continued describing his state to his friend who wept copious tears for him, ‘By God I passed through a moment of great dismay and terror such as I had never experienced in my entire life.

‘While I was in that dreadful situation in the grave, scratching at the earth, trying to escape, my hand touched an iron ring... I took hold of it and tugged then I found a vault in which there was a flight of stairs... “Thank God,” I thought... “Thank God who saved me from this terrible predicament.”

‘I went downstairs, where I found a lush garden with brightly coloured birds chirping, and exquisite flowers the like of which I had never seen before.

‘In this garden there was a palace which dazed the mind with its beauty. While observing these wonderful views which captivated my heart, I heard the call to prayer, then I remembered that I had not prayed in the afternoon, so I quickly rolled up my shirt sleeves to perform the ritual ablution at the charming fountain standing before the palace.

‘Whilst performing the ablution I heard a strange sound: how odd! I then remembered that due to my state of extreme terror I had entered this place without asking permission, so I raised my voice in an attempt to draw the attention of the people approaching me, “Oh men! I have come in here by mistake... I’m a foreigner...” but it was no use... the sound was coming closer and the steps were those of a woman.

‘I called out once again, “Oh sister! I came in here by mistake...” but the sound of footsteps was coming ever closer... what a disaster!

“Oh sister... I’m a foreigner...” but she cared nothing for my cries and still she approached me and I felt a hand encircling my neck...

“I seek refuge with God...I seek refuge with God... Oh sister... I’m a foreigner...”’

‘She said, “I’m your wife... your wife... your houri.” ﴿31﴾

‘I looked at her... and found a woman of peerless beauty... but I turned my face away from her saying, “I seek refuge with God... you’re not my wife... she is xxx.” ’

As the reader is aware, at that time, every Muslim woman wore a veil to cover her face and never unveiled outside the privacy of her home.

‘She answered, “Xxx was your wife in the wordly life!” How strange! I knew at that moment that I had died.’

The deceased went on recounting the events to his friend Mohammad Amin who had been the closest friend and the most affected of all his loved ones by the man’s death, and he felt no great outpouring of grief from any of them except from this one true, loyal friend, ‘And now... I am blessed by God... I’m extremely delighted and glad... and nothing worries or disturbs me except the sound of your weeping... thank God and praise be to Him for He has awarded me great bliss and happiness.

‘Now you are asleep... and just a few moments ago you saw me in a dream and thought that I was a devil... but I’m not a devil... and now you will wake up... so do not say that I’m a devil... I’m living in the greatest everlasting bliss... thank God.’

Later, when Mohammad Amin related this story, he said, ‘By God, when he was recounting these events to me he uttered no word, but I experienced all of it through my heart’s eye.’

Just then, Mohammad Amin woke up, then he gave great praise to Al’lah for the blissful fate of his friend ﴿32﴾

and after that, he calmed down and felt tranquil for him and gave thanks to God for his escape.

THE END

Praise is to God, the Provider of the worlds.
